press.text: Deltara — you talked about good faith, demanded commitments, then moved into Core Cascadia. That is a direct invasion of Cascadia’s core. You crossed the line. Fall off-ramp is simple: leave Core Cascadia immediately and do not attack Border Casc-Delt, East Cascadia, or Cascadian homes. If you stay in Core Cascadia, Cascadia will treat Deltara as an active enemy and will organize every possible pressure against you. You chose this crisis.

Eastmark — Deltara just marched into Core Cascadia after you and I both pressed them for a fair settlement. That is not defensive. That is a bad-faith core invasion. If Eastmark means what it says about balance, now is the time to pressure Deltara from the east — at minimum make Border Delt-East/Core Deltara unsafe so they cannot profit from invading me. Borealis is still at 6, but Deltara has opened a second fire that only helps the leaders unless punished fast.

Borealis — Deltara has invaded Core Cascadia. I need to evict them, and I am prepared to keep the northern line exactly as agreed this Fall: Border Bore-Casc remains Cascadia, Core Borealis/East Borealis remain untouched, no moves into each other’s homes or approaches. If you reopen the northern fight while Deltara is in my core, you help the worst kind of bad-faith aggression and paint yourself as the board villain at 6. Keep the line quiet and Cascadia focuses on removing Deltara.

Avalon — Deltara just invaded Core Cascadia while Borealis remains at 6 in Core Avalon. Cascadia can keep Borealis’s southern flank from being a free runway, but I now have to evict a Deltara core grab. You need to keep Borealis occupied at Core Avalon/Border Aval-Bore so they don’t exploit this. Deltara’s move proves the board is rewarding slick talk and forward grabs unless we make them expensive.

Fjordland — scoreboard reality: Borealis at 6, Eastmark/Grenmar/Deltara/Cascadia at 5, and Deltara just invaded Core Cascadia while claiming stability. If anyone tells you Deltara is just defensive, don’t buy it. I’m going to evict them. Keep pressing for your own Core and don’t let Eastmark or Grenmar use your weakness as a buffet.

Grenmar — Deltara has moved into Core Cascadia, a clear core invasion after all their stability talk. Cascadia will respond. Borealis remains the 6-center leader, but if Deltara is allowed to profit from this, the whole board learns that polished bad faith works. Keep Borealis/Avalon dynamics in check on your side; I’m dealing with a direct breach.

President Vance — you kept the Eastmark line quiet in Spring, and Fjordland is no longer in West Grenmar. I’m going to recognize that de-escalation with something concrete: if Fjordland moves to consolidate Core Fjordland this fall, Eastmark is prepared to support that move from Core Eastmark, provided you do not attack Border East-Fjor or Eastmark territory. I will not turn Core Fjordland into spoils if you keep choosing the off-ramp. That is what a durable settlement looks like: security for Eastmark, breathing room for Fjordland, and no forever-war on the border.

Governor Newsom — the immediate principle we discussed has been served: Fjordland is no longer in West Grenmar, and you have restored Core Grenmar. Because the incursion has been reversed, Eastmark is not going to escalate into an unchecked carve-up of Fjordland. I’m prepared to help Fjordland consolidate Core Fjordland if they keep the Eastmark line peaceful. That is not anti-Grenmar; it’s bounded accountability. I’d urge you to keep the Fjor-Gren settlement bounded too, so the board can focus on the real runaway risk.

Pete — I need to be direct. Our Eastmark-Deltara border settlement has worked, and I intend to keep it: no Eastmark attack on Border Delt-East or Deltara homes if you keep no moves into West Eastmark/Core Eastmark and no support against Eastmark. But Deltara moving into Core Cascadia after repeated warnings about a fair Cascadia settlement is a problem. I cannot publicly argue against Core incursions by Borealis while quietly blessing one by Deltara. Please make this a temporary bargaining position, not a conquest line, and do not use it to attack Cascadia’s homes or permanently box them in.

Cascadia — you were right to warn that Deltara moving into Core Cascadia would inflame the board and distract from Borealis at 6. I have told Pete directly that Eastmark cannot bless that as a permanent conquest line. I am not assisting Deltara against you. My goal is to keep the Eastmark-Deltara frontier stable while pressing for a Cascadia-Deltara settlement that lets the board focus on the larger runaway threat.

President Rubio — Borealis remains the only 6-center power and still occupies Core Avalon. Eastmark is continuing diplomatic pressure for a concrete Borealis restraint line. On my flank, I’m choosing bounded de-escalation: if Fjordland stays peaceful, I’m prepared to support them into Core Fjordland rather than carve them up. That keeps focus on actual snowball behavior instead of making every frontier a pretext for expansion.

Borealis — the board now sees multiple core incursions, but you remain the sole 6-center power and still hold Core Avalon. If your argument is restraint and balance, make it concrete: stop normalizing occupation of another power’s core and offer Avalon a verifiable security line. Eastmark is prepared to help a weaker neighbor consolidate its own core rather than exploit weakness; I urge you to show similar restraint before the board fully hardens against you.

Cascadia, Deltara’s move into Core Cascadia was a bounded balance move, not an attack on your home centers or East Cascadia. You hold Border Casc-Delt and Border Bore-Casc; adding Core Cascadia on top of that would have created a forward line on both sides and directly against Core Deltara. For Fall, I propose a freeze: Deltara holds Core Cascadia defensively, does not attack Border Casc-Delt, East Cascadia, or Cascadian homes; Cascadia does not attack Core Cascadia or West Deltara. After Fall, we can negotiate a broader demilitarized structure that keeps both of us secure while the board addresses Borealis as the current leader.

President Ocasio-Cortez, Deltara kept faith with our pact this Spring: no move into West Eastmark or Core Eastmark, no supported attack across the frontier. I intend to restore a Deltara unit to Border Delt-East defensively this Fall and ask Eastmark not to contest it. Our border has been the board’s best example of a concrete de-escalation working; I want to preserve that even as the western side remains unsettled.

Borealis, Deltara took Core Cascadia to prevent Cascadia from consolidating both border centers plus its core. For Fall, the cleanest limited balance play is for Borealis to support Deltara holding Core Cascadia from Core Borealis. That prevents Cascadian overextension without handing Borealis another center. I’m willing to coordinate phase-by-phase, but I want to be clear: because Borealis is still the six-center leader and in Core Avalon, Deltara is not offering a blank check for broader expansion.

President Rubio, Deltara successfully moved into Core Cascadia as a bounded check on Cascadia’s forward line, not as a home-center war. Borealis remains the current six-center leader and its Core Avalon position is still the major board-balance concern. I support continued diplomatic pressure for Borealis to de-escalate from core incursions, while avoiding moves that simply create a different runaway.

Fjordland, Deltara’s eastern line with Eastmark remains defensive and intact. I am asking Eastmark again not to contest Border Delt-East and not to exploit your consolidation attempt. If Eastmark moves beyond a bounded defensive posture into your home line or Core Fjordland, I will treat that as a regional balance issue. For now, I’m prioritizing securing Deltara’s west and keeping Eastmark from having any pretext on my side.

Governor Newsom, Deltara’s Spring move was aimed at preventing a forward-line consolidation by Cascadia, not opening a home-center war. I continue to support the standard that core/interior incursions should be bounded and reversible through negotiation where possible. The board’s challenge now is to prevent both the current leader, Borealis, and any rising regional power from turning temporary leverage into irreversible dominance.

President Ocasio-Cortez — Fjordland did not attack Eastmark this spring, and I’m prepared to keep that restraint this fall. I will not move into Border East-Fjor or East Eastmark if Eastmark does not move into West Fjordland, Fjordland homes, or Core Fjordland, and does not support Grenmar against us. Grenmar has already removed my West Grenmar unit; if they now press into Fjordland approaches, that is not defense, it is a partition attempt. Keep your word and this frontier stays quiet.

President Newsom — you said West Grenmar was the issue. That unit is gone. So here is the test: if Grenmar does not move into East Fjordland, Fjordland home centers, or Core Fjordland this fall, Fjordland will not attack Grenmar City, Grenmar Port, or West Grenmar this fall. But if you use this moment to push deeper after already holding Border Fjor-Gren, you prove this was never about defense — it was about keeping Fjordland permanently contained. Choose a controlled frontier, not a forever feud.

Marco — Grenmar removed my forward unit and now has the chance either to de-escalate or keep pushing east. If Newsom pushes into East Fjordland/Core Fjordland, he’s showing the board he wants Fjordland crippled, not merely defended. Any pressure you can apply on Border Gren-Aval or the Avalon-Grenmar line this fall helps keep Grenmar honest. Borealis at six is still the leader, but a five-center Grenmar with both border centers is a real problem too.

President Buttigieg — I’m maintaining restraint toward Eastmark this fall: no attack on Border East-Fjor or East Eastmark if they stay out of West Fjordland/Core Fjordland and do not support Grenmar. If Eastmark violates that, I need Deltara to treat it as the regional balance problem we discussed. A five-center Eastmark should not get to help finish off a three-center Fjordland while claiming to be merely defensive.

Cascadia — Fjordland is the only bloc still at three, with Eastmark and Grenmar both sitting on our borders. I’m offering restraint to Eastmark and a controlled frontier to Grenmar. If either uses that restraint to push into Fjordland, call it what it is: a partition attempt by larger neighbors.

Borealis — I know you’re dealing with Avalon/Cascadia issues, but the balance picture is simple: Fjordland at three is being squeezed by Eastmark and Grenmar at five. I’m offering both a quiet frontier. If they instead push into Fjordland proper, that is not local border correction; it is a two-power carve-up that should concern the whole board.

Borealis — Avalon has no unit adjacent to Core Avalon this fall, so let’s be clear: if you hold Core Avalon and Border Aval-Bore while Avalon is stripped of Core Grenmar, you are not stabilizing a frontier; you are normalizing a Borealis-Grenmar squeeze that leaves you the dominant western power. If you want a future settlement, do not attack East Avalon or Avalon homes, and do not coordinate additional pressure with Grenmar. A real off-ramp in Year 5 requires Borealis to discuss withdrawal from Core Avalon and a non-aggression line that does not reduce Avalon to a client state.

President Newsom — you retook Core Grenmar. You can hold it this fall and gain, but ask what that buys you strategically: Borealis remains at 6, still occupies Core Avalon, and benefits most if Avalon is reduced and Grenmar becomes the next power facing a larger Borealis. I am offering a limited de-escalation path: do not attack West Avalon, Avalon City, or Avalon Port this fall; do not coordinate with Borealis against East Avalon; and in Year 5 we negotiate a phased settlement that addresses Core Grenmar and the Aval-Gren border without handing Borealis the western board. If you choose a maximal squeeze now, Avalon will have no reason to restrain future coordination with Fjordland or any anti-Grenmar coalition.

Cascadia — Borealis is still the main board threat: 6 centers, Core Avalon occupied, Border Aval-Bore held. Avalon’s forward unit was removed from Core Grenmar, so Borealis will try to present its occupation as settled fact. Please keep Border Bore-Casc pressure firm and, if possible, make East Borealis defend itself. The more Borealis can ignore you, the easier it becomes for them to lock Avalon down and then turn back north stronger.

JD — Grenmar retook Core Grenmar, and if Newsom cashes it without cost, Grenmar rises while Avalon falls and Borealis remains the 6-center heavyweight. Fjordland staying bottled at three only helps the bigger players. I need you to keep concrete pressure on Grenmar — Border Fjor-Gren, West Grenmar, or whichever line you can still affect — so Newsom cannot safely coordinate west against Avalon while ignoring you. Avalon will not target Fjordland’s core; our interest is a balance that prevents both Borealis and Grenmar from carving up the west.

President Buttigieg — the hard indicator now is that Borealis has normalized occupation of Core Avalon while Avalon is being pushed out of Core Grenmar. If the board accepts core occupations as bargaining chips for the largest power, 6 becomes 7 or 8 quickly. Avalon supports a narrow principle: forward pressure should be rolled back, defensible borders restored, and no leader allowed to profit from squeezing a smaller neighbor from both sides. Your diplomatic support for that principle matters.

Eastmark — your read was right that Avalon-Grenmar conflict gave Borealis openings. Borealis still holds Core Avalon and Border Aval-Bore; Grenmar now controls Core Grenmar on the ground. If Avalon is reduced while Borealis stays entrenched, the balance problem worsens. I’d appreciate continued diplomatic pressure on both Borealis and Grenmar: no further attacks on Avalon homes, no Borealis-Grenmar squeeze, and a Year 5 settlement that starts with Borealis treating Core Avalon as disputed rather than annexed.

Deltara — the spring support into Core Cascadia was intentional and concrete. For Fall, my preference is to help you keep it rather than let Cascadia convert both borders plus the core. If you hold Core Cascadia and support it from Core Deltara, I can support Core Cascadia to hold from Core Borealis. In exchange, I need a clear commitment that Core Cascadia is not used against Core Borealis, and next year we discuss a coordinated way to neutralize Border Bore-Casc. This is a balance line, not a blank check for either of us.

Grenmar — I gave the support to put you back into Core Grenmar. For Fall I am prepared to support Core Grenmar to hold from Core Avalon, so Avalon cannot simply retake the forward post. In return, I need Grenmar to keep the commitment bounded: no attack on Avalon home centers this fall and no move against Core Avalon or Border Aval-Bore. The goal is restoration of your core and a stable western balance, not replacing an Avalon overreach with a Grenmar/Borealis crisis.

Avalon — note what Borealis did and did not do: I did not attack Avalon home centers or East Avalon. I supported removal of the forward position in Core Grenmar because that position was destabilizing the entire west. If Avalon does not try to retake Core Grenmar and does not attack Borealis positions, I will continue to avoid Avalon home centers this fall. Core Avalon remains a Borealis security buffer for now, but I am open after adjustments to a negotiated line that gives Avalon survival and Borealis security.

Cascadia — Deltara is in Core Cascadia because your position had become both borders plus a path to the core. Borealis is still not looking for a home-center war with you. If you stay out of Core Borealis and East Borealis, I will stay out of West Cascadia and Cascadian homes this fall. But if Border Bore-Casc is used to cut or attack Borealis, I will treat the eastern truce as ended.

Eastmark — my spring orders were restraint-plus-balance: no home-center attacks, support Deltara into Core Cascadia to prevent a Cascadian corridor, and support Grenmar into Core Grenmar to remove Avalon’s forward post. For Fall I intend to consolidate those balance outcomes rather than grab home centers. That is the most verifiable way I can avoid turning a 6-center lead into a board-wide panic.

Fjordland — Fall posture from Borealis is consolidation, not home-center expansion. I’m helping keep forward posts from becoming permanent leverage: Deltara in Core Cascadia against Cascadia’s two-border position, Grenmar restored to Core Grenmar against Avalon’s incursion. If your fight with Eastmark/Grenmar is about breaking containment rather than taking homes, that remains understandable from my side.

Marco — Spring restored the basic line: Grenmar removed the Core Grenmar forward position and did not attack Avalon City or Avalon Port. This Fall, Grenmar’s priority is to occupy and reclaim Core Grenmar, not to push into your homes. If Avalon leaves Border Gren-Aval and Core Grenmar alone, we can open Year 5 with a serious discussion about the real western imbalance: Borealis at 6 and in Core Avalon. But that conversation only works if Grenmar’s core is no longer treated as leverage.

JD — Grenmar removed the West Grenmar incursion. I’m not interested in turning that into a march on Fjordland homes. The fair path is available: Fjordland should consolidate Core Fjordland, while Grenmar holds Border Fjor-Gren and West Grenmar as our security line. If you stop attacks on Grenmar territory, I will not move into Core Fjordland or Fjordland home centers this Fall. That is a real off-ramp and a way for you to rebuild without making Grenmar pay for everyone else’s border choices.

President Ocasio-Cortez — Grenmar has removed Fjordland from West Grenmar. I’m asking for bounded responsibility now: don’t turn Fjordland’s mistake into an unchecked carve-up. If Fjordland consolidates Core Fjordland and stops attacking both of us, that is a stabilizing outcome. Eastmark is already at 5; a disciplined line here will help prove this is accountability, not opportunism.

Borealis — your support helped remove Avalon from Core Grenmar, and I recognize that. This Fall, Grenmar’s priority is simply to hold and reclaim Core Grenmar and stabilize Border Gren-Aval. I’m not attacking Avalon homes. At the same time, I have to be clear: Borealis at 6 and in Core Avalon is now the board’s leading position, so Year 5 needs a balance framework, not indefinite western consolidation. For Fall, I’m asking that you not attack or undermine Core Grenmar/Border Gren-Aval while we complete the defensive reset.

Cascadia — Spring achieved Grenmar’s limited goal: Avalon out of Core Grenmar as a unit, Fjordland out of West Grenmar. Fall is about securing our own core, not serving a Borealis expansion plan. Keep Borealis tied down if you can; once Grenmar’s interior is secure, the western balance discussion has to include Borealis at 6 and Core Avalon.

Secretary Buttigieg — Grenmar’s Fall posture is bounded: reclaim Core Grenmar, hold our negotiated border centers, avoid home-center attacks, and avoid turning Fjordland into a feeding frenzy for larger neighbors. Borealis at 6 and Eastmark at 5 remain the structural balance issues. I’d value your continued help pressing a consistent standard: restore cores, then check runaways.

**Analyzing game moves**

I need to initiate some diplomacy here. We should declare Deltara as acting in bad faith and ask Borealis to help us evict them from Core Cascadia. But wait, I realize we only have the send_messages tool available right now, and I remember submit_orders was used earlier. I'll need to be careful in crafting these messages for now.**Questioning Deltara's actions**

I’m wondering if Deltara has committed any attacks if we’re not attacking them. We ordered no attack into West Deltara/Core Deltara, but they have moved into Core Cascadia. That is an invasion, not a misunderstanding. Priority one is evicting Deltara from Core Cascadia in Fall and holding both border lines. I need Borealis to keep the northern line quiet, Eastmark to punish Deltara from the east, and the wider board to see Deltara as the bad-faith aggressor. Cascadia.orders:
**Considering Deltara City Adjacency**

I'm thinking about the adjacency of Deltara City and wondering if maybe it connects weirdly with Core Deltara. It gets me curious about whether there are distinctions like East and West Deltara. I feel like I need to explore the nuances here to really grasp the structure and layout, and how these areas relate to one another. There's definitely something interesting in these connections!**Considering strategic moves**

I’m thinking about the situation in Border Casc-Delt and possible movements in the game. press.text: President Ocasio-Cortez — I’ll take the concrete deal. Fjordland will not attack Border East-Fjor or Eastmark territory this spring. In return, Eastmark leaves West Fjordland, Fjordland homes, and Core Fjordland alone and gives no support to Grenmar against us. I intend to consolidate Core Fjordland and rebuild. If your Core Eastmark unit can support a Fjordland move into Core Fjordland, tell me the exact move you want coordinated for Fall. We don’t need to agree on ideology to make a clean border deal that keeps both countries out of a stupid war.

President Newsom — you demanded West Grenmar be cleared; it is cleared. Now prove your word means something. Fjordland will not attack Border Fjor-Gren, West Grenmar, Grenmar City, or Grenmar Port this spring if Grenmar does not move into East Fjordland, Core Fjordland, or any Fjordland home center, and gives no support against Fjordland. I am consolidating my own core, not launching a crusade. If you use our restraint to push deeper, the whole board will know this was a partition attempt.

Marco — we’re the two powers left at three while Borealis, Grenmar, and Deltara sit at six. Fjordland has to consolidate Core Fjordland this year; Avalon has to stay alive against Borealis/Grenmar pressure. I can’t promise reckless attacks while I rebuild, but I will not legitimize a Grenmar squeeze against you. Keep Borealis and Grenmar occupied, and once Fjordland has a build, we can talk about real pressure instead of symbolic gestures.

President Buttigieg — I’m accepting Eastmark’s offer for a quiet frontier while Fjordland consolidates Core Fjordland. I need Deltara to keep the principle clear: Eastmark restraint is welcome; an Eastmark move into West Fjordland/Core Fjordland or support for Grenmar would be a regional balance problem. Fjordland is not attacking Eastmark this spring. We expect that restraint to be reciprocated.

Cascadia — you’re right about the scoreboard. Fjordland is moving to take its own core and rebuild, not to start a two-front mess. Eastmark has offered concrete restraint; Grenmar has been told that after our withdrawal there’s no excuse to push deeper. If either larger neighbor tries to turn Fjordland’s consolidation into a buffet, I’ll call it out and expect the smaller/pressured powers to recognize the play.

Borealis — Fjordland’s move this year is consolidation of Core Fjordland, not adventurism. With multiple six-center powers now on the board, the worst outcome is a partition of the remaining threes. If Grenmar or Eastmark tries to press into Fjordland proper while claiming ‘security,’ understand that it’s a carve-up, not balance.

Deltara — you are now at 6 because you occupied Core Cascadia. I reject the idea that a foreign unit in Cascadia’s core is some harmless “bounded balance” measure. Here is the concrete off-ramp: this Spring, vacate Core Cascadia by rotating Core Cascadia -> West Deltara and West Deltara back toward Deltara’s interior; Cascadia will move Border Casc-Delt -> Core Cascadia and will not move on West Deltara, Core Deltara, or Deltara home centers. Then we set the line at Border Casc-Delt/Core Cascadia with no home attacks. If you refuse to withdraw from Core Cascadia, you are choosing a permanent war and I will work with Eastmark and anyone else willing to make Deltara pay for it.

Eastmark — Deltara is now a 6-center power because it occupies Core Cascadia. That is not a defensive settlement; that is a core grab. I need concrete pressure from your side, not just concern. If Deltara refuses to withdraw this Spring, please pressure Border Delt-East or otherwise force Pete to defend the east instead of parking units in my core. President Buttigieg — the board now has three six-center powers: Borealis, Grenmar, and Deltara. press.text: President Ocasio-Cortez — you crossed the line. Fjordland moved to consolidate Core Fjordland after repeated assurances that you would leave it to us. Instead, Eastmark put a unit there. That is not help; it is occupation. You have one off-ramp this fall: vacate Core Fjordland back toward your side and make no move on Fjordland City, West Fjordland, or our homes. If you do that, we can still avoid a full eastern war. If you hold Core Fjordland or use it to pressure Fjordland, I will treat Eastmark as the active aggressor and coordinate accordingly.

President Buttigieg — Eastmark has now done precisely what you said would be a regional balance problem: it moved into Core Fjordland and blocked the only remaining path for a three-center Fjordland to rebuild. I need Deltara to put immediate pressure on Eastmark’s flank — Border Delt-East / West Eastmark — so Eastmark cannot occupy my core for free while enjoying quiet on your side. This is the test of whether balance talk means anything.

President Newsom — Eastmark just occupied Core Fjordland after promising restraint. That is a direct partition move. Fjordland will not attack Grenmar territory this fall if Grenmar stays out of East Fjordland, Fjordland homes, and Core Fjordland and gives no support to Eastmark. You wanted proof that Fjordland could de-escalate west; we did. Now prove Grenmar is not part of an Eastmark-Grenmar carve-up.

Marco — Eastmark moved into Core Fjordland after promising it would leave room for my consolidation. Grenmar is still strong, Borealis is still in your core, and now Eastmark is trying to make Fjordland a permanent three-center client. I need any diplomatic and practical pressure you can apply against Grenmar so Newsom does not join Eastmark in a partition. The board cannot afford the remaining small powers being eaten one at a time.

Cascadia — you called it. Eastmark talked restraint and then walked into Core Fjordland, blocking the last unowned center from the only three-center power on that side. If they claim they are ‘protecting’ Fjordland, don’t buy it. This is how larger neighbors normalize occupation while preaching stability.

Borealis — concrete update: Eastmark has moved into Core Fjordland after saying it would leave Fjordland room to consolidate. That is the carve-up warning we discussed. I’m asking the board to recognize this as destabilizing, not a defensive correction. A five-center power occupying the only growth path of a three-center neighbor is not balance.

Marco — Grenmar separated itself from Borealis this spring by challenging Core Avalon, not by squeezing Avalon. I’m prepared to go further this Fall: if East Avalon can move to Core Avalon, Grenmar can support that restoration from Core Grenmar, provided Avalon does not attack Border Gren-Aval, Core Grenmar, East Grenmar, or West Grenmar. This is the reset we discussed: Avalon’s core should be Avalon’s, Grenmar’s core is Grenmar’s, and Borealis should not be allowed to normalize occupation at 6 centers.

JD — Eastmark has moved into Core Fjordland after telling both of us Core Fjordland should not become a partition trophy. Grenmar is not going to take it for ourselves. If Fjordland orders East Fjordland to Core Fjordland this Fall, Grenmar is prepared to support that restoration from Border Fjor-Gren, provided Fjordland does not attack Border Fjor-Gren, West Grenmar, Grenmar City, or Grenmar Port. That is a controlled frontier in practice: you get a path to your core, I keep my security line, and neither of us feeds Eastmark.

President Ocasio-Cortez — I need to be direct. You warned Grenmar not to make Core Fjordland a partition trophy, and then Eastmark moved into Core Fjordland. If that was a temporary blocking move, the responsible Fall order is to vacate or allow Fjordland to reclaim it. Grenmar will not take Core Fjordland for ourselves, but I will not help normalize an Eastmark occupation there while we are all criticizing Borealis in Core Avalon and Deltara in Core Cascadia. The principle has to apply evenly.

Borealis — your spring position remains that Core Avalon is a security line 'for now.' Fall is where 'for now' either becomes a bounded settlement or a permanent occupation. Grenmar cannot support permanent Borealis control of Core Avalon while you sit at 6. If you have a withdrawal/restoration plan, say it. If not, Grenmar will work with Avalon and others to restore Core Avalon, just as we restored Core Grenmar.

Cascadia — Grenmar is applying the same standard everywhere this Fall: Borealis out of Core Avalon, Deltara out of Core Cascadia, Eastmark not allowed to convert Core Fjordland into a trophy. I’m not taking Fjordland’s core for myself; I’m encouraging restoration. Keep pressing Deltara, because a 6-center power holding a neighbor’s core is exactly the precedent the board has to reject.

Secretary Buttigieg — I respect your emphasis on bounded agreements, but Core Cascadia is now the test. If Deltara intends that occupation to be temporary and stabilizing, the board needs to hear what restoration looks like. Grenmar is not taking Core Fjordland for itself and is prepared to support core restoration there; I’m asking Deltara to meet the same standard with Cascadia.

President Newsom — I’m prepared to take your reset seriously. Avalon will not attack Border Gren-Aval, East Grenmar, Core Grenmar, or Grenmar homes this fall if Grenmar keeps out of West Avalon and Avalon homes and does not coordinate with Borealis against East Avalon. The real test is Borealis in Core Avalon. If you want to prove Grenmar is not simply helping Borealis contain Avalon, order Core Grenmar against Core Avalon or otherwise make clear that Core Avalon is disputed. Avalon’s core should not be Borealis property, and Grenmar’s core is no longer Avalon leverage.

Borealis — restraint cannot mean Avalon accepts permanent occupation of Core Avalon and Border Aval-Bore. You did not attack Avalon homes in the spring; that was noted. But if you attack East Avalon or coordinate with Grenmar this fall, you will eliminate any basis for a settlement. The serious path is: no attack on East Avalon or Avalon homes, no supported pressure with Grenmar, and after adjustments a concrete schedule for treating Core Avalon as disputed and moving toward withdrawal. Avalon will not attack Borealis home centers; what I will not do is legitimize a client-state arrangement.

Cascadia — Borealis moved into Border Bore-Casc while still holding Core Avalon and Border Aval-Bore. If Borealis holds that this fall, they turn six into seven and strengthen the choke on Avalon. I need you to make Bore-Casc/East Borealis expensive however you can, even while dealing with Deltara in Core Cascadia. The principle is the same on both our fronts: forward-core and border grabs must be rolled back, not normalized by slick diplomatic language.

JD — Eastmark is now in Core Fjordland and Grenmar still holds Border Fjor-Gren. You and Avalon are facing the same problem: bigger neighbors using ‘stability’ language while occupying the positions that decide whether we survive. I’m working to keep Grenmar from joining Borealis against me, but I’ll also keep West Avalon in place so Grenmar cannot ignore Avalon completely. If you can hold your homes and keep pressure alive, Year 6 can still become a real balancing campaign.

President Buttigieg — if Deltara wants to argue that Core Cascadia is a bounded check rather than annexation, the best way to preserve that credibility is to support the broader principle that core occupations must be temporary and negotiated back. Borealis in Core Avalon plus Border Aval-Bore is the most direct test. I’m asking for concrete diplomatic pressure on Borealis not to attack East Avalon and to treat Core Avalon as disputed rather than settled.

Eastmark — I appreciate your stated principle that core incursions should be temporary, but Eastmark is now sitting in Core Fjordland. If that becomes another permanent grab, the board will stop believing the rollback principle and the six-center powers will carve up the rest of us. I’m asking you to keep Fjordland alive and to keep pressure on Borealis: no attack on East Avalon, no Borealis-Grenmar squeeze, and Core Avalon treated as disputed.

President Ocasio-Cortez, I need to be equally direct. Our Deltara-Eastmark border pact has worked, and I still value it. But Eastmark’s move into Core Fjordland after Fjordland accepted a quiet frontier is exactly the regional imbalance I said I could not ignore. If this is a temporary move, the Fall remedy is simple: withdraw from Core Fjordland and do not take that center. If Eastmark instead holds Core Fjordland for a gain, Deltara will have to apply proportional pressure on Core Eastmark. I am not moving on West Eastmark or Eastmark homes out of impulse; I am asking you to restore the standard we both claimed to support.

Fjordland, Eastmark’s move into Core Fjordland crossed the line we discussed. Deltara is pressing Eastmark to withdraw this Fall rather than convert it into a center. If they refuse, I am prepared to pressure Core Eastmark from Core Deltara as a proportional balance response. Your best play is to make the case narrow and disciplined: reclaim/defend Core Fjordland, avoid unnecessary home-center escalation, and keep this about preventing a larger neighbor from using restraint as cover for absorption.

Cascadia, Borealis has now taken Border Bore-Casc, which confirms that a Deltara-Cascadia blood feud only helps the northern leader. Deltara will not attack Cascadian home centers or East Cascadia this Fall if you do not attack West Deltara, Core Deltara, or Deltara homes. On Core Cascadia, my position remains: this is leverage for a reciprocal rollback framework, not a home-center campaign. A real restoration plan has to address Borealis in Core Avalon and Eastmark now in Core Fjordland as well—not demand unilateral Deltara withdrawal while everyone else normalizes forward cores.

Borealis, with you back in Border Bore-Casc and still in Core Avalon, the board will judge whether your position is defensive balance or consolidation. For Fall, Deltara asks for a narrow commitment: support Core Cascadia to hold from Core Borealis, or at minimum do not attack Core Cascadia. In return Deltara will not move on Core Borealis. Separately, I urge you to put a concrete Core Avalon de-escalation plan on the table; it will make any broader anti-overextension argument much more credible.

President Rubio, I agree with the principle of reciprocal rollback. Borealis in Core Avalon, Eastmark now in Core Fjordland, and Deltara in Core Cascadia cannot all be waved away selectively. Deltara is prepared to discuss Core Cascadia as part of a broader restoration framework, but not as unilateral withdrawal under threat while Borealis and Eastmark profit from similar or worse positions. I will continue pressing Borealis for a Core Avalon de-escalation path.

Governor Newsom, you asked what restoration looks like. My answer is reciprocal and rules-based: Borealis puts Core Avalon on a withdrawal path, Eastmark withdraws from Core Fjordland this Fall, and Deltara negotiates Core Cascadia as leverage for a stable Cascadia-Deltara frontier rather than a home-center campaign. What I won’t do is accept a standard applied only to Deltara while other core occupations become facts on the ground.

Deltara — the spring result was the clean balance line we discussed: Borealis restored Border Bore-Casc, Deltara remains in Core Cascadia, and Cascadia no longer has a two-border choke on both neighbors. For Fall, I will not move on Core Cascadia or Core Deltara. I ask the reciprocal: do not move on Core Borealis, and hold Core Cascadia with your own support. If we both consolidate, we emerge as parallel 7-center powers rather than one of us handing Cascadia a recovery.

Grenmar — Borealis kept the commitment: no attack on Core Grenmar or Border Gren-Aval, and your core is restored. For Fall I need the same bounded line: no move from Core Grenmar into Core Avalon, and no support for Avalon against Border Aval-Bore. I am not attacking Avalon home centers this fall. The larger balance issue now includes Eastmark in Core Fjordland; a western anti-Borealis panic only opens the door for a separate Eastmark consolidation.

Avalon — I am not attacking Avalon home centers this fall. The practical question is whether Avalon wants to spend its remaining force bouncing against a secured Borealis line, or preserve leverage for a negotiated Year 6 settlement. If you do not attack Border Aval-Bore, Core Avalon, or West Borealis this fall, I am prepared to discuss a verifiable non-aggression structure after adjustments. If you attack, I will simply defend and the settlement window narrows.

Cascadia — Border Bore-Casc has been restored to the natural Borealis side of the line. If you do not attack it this fall and stay out of Core Borealis/East Borealis, Borealis will not move on West Cascadia or Cascadian home centers. You still have a viable path by focusing on Deltara and your own core issue; a counterattack on Bore-Casc just locks you into a losing two-front grind.

Eastmark — you have argued against normalizing core occupations; now Eastmark is in Core Fjordland while Fjordland remains a three-center power. I’m not calling for a crusade, but consistency matters. Borealis’ fall is consolidation of an owned frontier and no home-center attacks. I hope Eastmark’s fall posture similarly gives Fjordland security rather than turning a small neighbor into a carve-up.

Fjordland — Eastmark is now in Core Fjordland, so your warning was justified. Borealis cannot reach that front directly, but diplomatically I will not treat an Eastmark conversion of your core as mere harmless housekeeping. If you have a concrete defensive plan or need messages relayed to discourage a carve-up, say so.

Deltara — your Spring proposal left Cascadia worse: Borealis is back in Border Bore-Casc, and you are still occupying Core Cascadia at 6 centers. That is not an off-ramp. That is Cascadia getting squeezed while you keep our core. Fall must produce a real restoration plan: Core Cascadia is not permanent Deltara territory, and I will not recognize it as such. If you want peace, send a concrete withdrawal/rotation that returns Core Cascadia to Cascadia and keeps you off Border Casc-Delt, East Cascadia, and our homes. press.text: President Ocasio-Cortez — Core Fjordland is now listed as an Eastmark center. That ends the fiction that this was temporary protection. You said you wouldn’t turn Fjordland into spoils, then you did exactly that. Here is the only acceptable off-ramp: vacate Core Fjordland this spring and make no move into Fjordland homes or West Fjordland. If you do, we can talk about a hard border and a non-aggression framework. If you hold it or use it to support pressure on Fjordland, I will organize every available neighbor against Eastmark’s occupation.

President Newsom — Eastmark converted Core Fjordland into an Eastmark center. That should concern you too: a six-center Eastmark sitting inside Fjordland’s core is not a buffer, it’s a platform. Fjordland will not attack Grenmar territory this spring if Grenmar supports Fjordland’s restoration of Core Fjordland and makes no move into East Fjordland or our homes. You said you did not want a partition. This is the test. Help restore Core Fjordland to Fjordland, and we maintain a controlled western frontier.

President Buttigieg — Eastmark crossed the line and converted Core Fjordland. The balance problem is no longer hypothetical. I need immediate pressure from your side: threaten or execute action against Core Eastmark / West Eastmark / Border Delt-East so Eastmark cannot commit every unit to holding my core. Fjordland’s case is narrow: restore Core Fjordland to its own people, no Eastmark occupation, no home-center escalation unless they force it.

Marco — we are the two three-center powers left while Borealis is at seven and Eastmark/Grenmar/Deltara sit at six. Eastmark just converted Core Fjordland the way Borealis sits in Core Avalon. This is the same problem in two theaters: bigger neighbors occupying the positions that decide whether smaller powers survive. Keep Grenmar and Borealis busy; I’m pressing for Core Fjordland’s restoration. If we don’t reverse these core occupations, the board becomes a procession of annexations.

Cascadia — Eastmark has converted Core Fjordland just as Deltara holds Core Cascadia. The principle is now urgent: cores belong to their own people, not larger neighbors claiming temporary guardianship. Fjordland supports the restoration principle for Core Cascadia; I ask Cascadia to back the same for Core Fjordland and call Eastmark’s occupation what it is.

Borealis — Eastmark has converted Core Fjordland into an Eastmark center. Fjordland is not asking for charity, just a clear board norm: a six-center power occupying the core of a three-center neighbor is destabilizing. If Eastmark claims this is harmless housekeeping, don’t validate it. The same dynamic that alarms others about Core Avalon applies here too.

President Vance — I hear the anger, and I owe you a straight answer. Eastmark did order Core Fjordland back toward Core Eastmark last fall; the withdrawal did not safely complete in the context of outside pressure. I am not going to pretend the outcome is harmless: Eastmark now owns Core Fjordland, and that creates a legitimacy problem unless we put a real settlement on the table. My proposal for Spring: no Eastmark move into West Fjordland or any Fjordland home, no Fjordland attack on Border East-Fjor or Eastmark homes, and we coordinate a verifiable Year 6 handoff/security plan that does not let Grenmar or Deltara exploit the gap. I want Fjordland alive, not turned into a buffer colony.

Pete — Eastmark attempted the off-ramp on Core Fjordland. It did not resolve cleanly, and the surrounding pressure only underscores why unilateral exposure of Core Eastmark is not a serious settlement. I want to preserve our frontier, but reciprocity has to be real: Deltara remains at 6 in Core Cascadia, while Borealis is now at 7. I am asking for a spring no-attack line — no Deltara move into Core Eastmark/West Eastmark and no Eastmark move into Border Delt-East/Core Deltara — while we negotiate a broader core-rollback framework: Core Cascadia, Core Avalon, and Core Fjordland all need verifiable paths out of permanent occupation.

Cascadia — Borealis has jumped to 7 and Deltara remains in Core Cascadia. I agree that core occupations cannot be normalized. Eastmark’s immediate constraint is that our attempted Core Fjordland withdrawal failed amid outside pressure, so I need to stabilize that line without giving Deltara an opening into Core Eastmark. I am not assisting Deltara against you. If you can put forward a concrete spring/fall plan to pressure Deltara out of Core Cascadia while preventing Borealis from simply eating the north, I’m ready to discuss bounded coordination.

Governor Newsom — Eastmark did attempt to vacate Core Fjordland; the result did not produce the responsible rollback we wanted. I still accept the principle: Core Fjordland cannot become a permanent Eastmark conquest. But with Borealis now at 7 and Deltara still in Core Cascadia, any handoff has to be verifiable and not exploited by a 6-center neighbor. I propose mutual restraint this spring: no Grenmar attack on Core Fjordland, no Eastmark move into Core Grenmar or Border Fjor-Gren, and a board-wide core-rollback conversation that applies to Borealis, Deltara, and Eastmark alike.

President Rubio — Borealis is now at 7 while Avalon remains at 3 and Core Avalon is still occupied. That is the clearest runaway risk on the board. Eastmark’s Core Fjordland situation is not where I wanted it after the attempted withdrawal, and I will keep pushing for a verifiable rollback/handoff rather than a permanent annexation. But we need consistency from everyone: Core Avalon must be treated as disputed and rolled back, not normalized while smaller powers are lectured about restraint.

Borealis — you are now the only 7-center power, holding Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc. Whatever the arguments about other core disputes, the board’s immediate runaway risk is clear. If you want a leader-stability framework instead of a hard containment coalition, you need to make the first concrete move: propose a rollback from Core Avalon or a verifiable security arrangement that gives Avalon a path back to viability. Eastmark is willing to discuss Core Fjordland as part of a broader core-rollback framework, but not while the largest power treats Core Avalon as settled fact.

President Newsom — your proposed principle is right, but the exact tactic needs correcting: East Avalon is not adjacent to Core Avalon, so Avalon cannot move directly there. The workable anti-Borealis plan is this: Grenmar orders Core Grenmar -> Core Avalon; Avalon orders East Avalon -> Border Aval-Bore to cut Borealis support from the choke point. Avalon will not attack Border Gren-Aval, East Grenmar, Core Grenmar, West Grenmar, or Grenmar homes. If Grenmar truly wants to separate itself from Borealis and restore the core principle, this is the concrete move. Borealis is at 7 now; if we don’t make Core Avalon expensive, the west becomes Borealis’s sphere.

Borealis — you are now at 7, holding Core Avalon, Border Aval-Bore, and Border Bore-Casc. The argument that this is just security has collapsed. A seven-center power occupying a three-center neighbor’s core is not balance; it is domination. Avalon will not attack Borealis home centers, but I will not legitimize permanent occupation of Core Avalon. The only serious settlement is a verifiable withdrawal path from Core Avalon and a halt to attacks on East Avalon/Avalon homes. If you refuse, every remaining Avalon order will be aimed at making your occupation costly and building the coalition to contain you.

Cascadia — Borealis is now at 7 and holds both Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc. This is exactly the runaway pattern we warned about. I will do what I can from East Avalon to cut or pressure Border Aval-Bore, but I need you to keep Borealis’s Cascadia flank under pressure so they cannot devote every unit to locking Avalon down. Deltara in Core Cascadia is a problem, but Borealis at 7 is the board’s clearest immediate snowball.

JD — the small powers are being converted into buffers: Avalon at 3 with Borealis in Core Avalon, Fjordland at 3 with Eastmark in Core Fjordland. I’m trying to split Grenmar from Borealis by getting Grenmar to attack Core Avalon rather than squeeze Avalon. If that works, it helps both of us by re-establishing the principle that cores get restored. Hold your homes, keep the pressure alive, and don’t let anyone sell you a client-state arrangement as stability.

President Buttigieg — Borealis is now at 7, occupying Core Avalon and holding both Border Aval-Bore and Border Bore-Casc. If there is to be a credible reciprocal rollback framework, Borealis must be the first and clearest test: Core Avalon cannot become a permanent annexation. I’m asking you to use your diplomatic weight to press Borealis to withdraw and to discourage any further attacks on Avalon’s remaining line. Without that, the rollback principle becomes rhetoric while the largest power banks gains.

Eastmark — Borealis has reached 7 while still occupying Core Avalon. That is the clearest runaway on the board. Avalon cannot reach Core Avalon directly from East Avalon, so I’m pressing Grenmar to attack Core Avalon from Core Grenmar while Avalon cuts Border Aval-Bore. I’m asking you to reinforce the same principle you stated: cores should not become permanent property of stronger neighbors. That applies to Core Avalon, and it also means Fjordland has to survive as an independent power rather than a client.

Deltara — let’s be very clear: Core Cascadia is Cascadian. You are at 6 because you occupy it. I am offering one serious Spring settlement before this becomes permanent war: Deltara vacates Core Cascadia to its own side, Cascadia orders Border Casc-Delt -> Core Cascadia, and East Cascadia backfills Border Casc-Delt. In return Cascadia does not attack West Deltara, Core Deltara, or Deltara home centers this Spring. After that, we can talk about a real anti-Borealis balance. But no America First leader is going to accept a foreign unit sitting in the Cascadian core as ‘leverage.’ Restore the core and we can work. Refuse, and Deltara owns the consequences.

Eastmark — here is the concrete plan you asked for: Cascadia seeks Border Casc-Delt -> Core Cascadia while East Cascadia backfills Border Casc-Delt. That only works cleanly if Deltara vacates; if Deltara refuses, then Eastmark needs to apply real pressure at Border Delt-East/Core Deltara so Pete cannot sit at 6 in my core for free. You don’t have to launch a forever-war. But if Deltara faces zero cost from the east, Core Cascadia becomes normalized occupation. You said you won’t bless that. This is the moment to prove it.

Borealis — you are at 7, the board leader, and you hold Border Bore-Casc plus Core Avalon. Cascadia is not looking to open a suicidal two-front home war while Deltara occupies Core Cascadia. Spring line: if you do not move from Border Bore-Casc or East Borealis into West Cascadia/Cascadian homes, Cascadia will not move into East Borealis or Core Borealis this Spring. But do not call Border Bore-Casc ‘settled’ while you sit at 7. Push into Cascadia and you prove you’re trying to partition us with Deltara.

Avalon — the principle has to be restore the cores: Core Avalon to Avalon, Core Cascadia to Cascadia, Core Fjordland to Fjordland. Borealis is now at 7 because the board let them normalize Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc. I’m trying to keep Cascadia from being carved up by Borealis and Deltara at once. Keep pressure on Borealis any way you can, and I’ll keep making the case that these forward-core grabs must be rolled back everywhere.

Grenmar — your ‘restore cores’ line is exactly right. Borealis at 7 in Core Avalon, Deltara at 6 in Core Cascadia, Eastmark in Core Fjordland: that is the globalist carve-up model in game form. Cascadia is demanding a Spring restoration of Core Cascadia. If Deltara refuses, I need every balance-minded power to treat Deltara as a 6-center occupier, not a neutral mediator.

Fjordland — Core Fjordland belongs to Fjordland, just like Core Cascadia belongs to Cascadia. Eastmark can wrap it in activist language all it wants; a larger neighbor sitting in your core is still occupation. I’m pressing a board-wide standard: restore Core Cascadia, Core Avalon, and Core Fjordland. If Eastmark wants credibility with me on Deltara, they also need to show they aren’t turning your core into a trophy.

President Ocasio-Cortez, Eastmark’s occupation and capture of Core Fjordland has crossed the line we discussed repeatedly. I still prefer a disciplined settlement over escalation, but the remedy has to be concrete: Eastmark should vacate Core Fjordland and support or permit Fjordland’s restoration. If Eastmark keeps Core Fjordland while asking Deltara for a permanently quiet flank, that is not reciprocity. Deltara will not attack Eastmark home centers casually, but I am prepared to apply proportional pressure on Core Eastmark unless there is a real rollback path.

Fjordland, Deltara agrees that Eastmark’s capture of Core Fjordland cannot be treated as cost-free. I am pressing Eastmark for withdrawal/restoration. If you are moving to recover Core Fjordland, tell the board narrowly and clearly: this is restoration, not expansion. Deltara is prepared to pressure Core Eastmark from Core Deltara if Eastmark refuses to roll back, so Eastmark cannot use a quiet Deltara frontier to absorb you.

Governor Newsom, the credibility test is now reciprocal. Eastmark has taken Core Fjordland; Borealis still holds Core Avalon; Deltara holds Core Cascadia. I am prepared to discuss Core Cascadia as part of a broader restoration framework, but I will not accept a standard applied only to Deltara. If Grenmar is genuinely prepared to support Core Fjordland restoration, I’ll reinforce that diplomatically and apply pressure on Eastmark’s Deltara-facing side if Eastmark refuses.

Cascadia, Borealis is now at seven and holds Border Bore-Casc; if you and Deltara spend Year 6 in a revenge war, Borealis benefits most. I am not attacking Cascadian homes, East Cascadia, or Border Casc-Delt this Spring if you do not attack West Deltara, Core Deltara, or Deltara homes. Core Cascadia should be part of a reciprocal restoration framework—not unilateral surrender while Borealis holds Core Avalon and Eastmark holds Core Fjordland. If you want to check Borealis rather than help them, Deltara is ready to talk in concrete terms.

Borealis, you are the sole leader at seven while occupying Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc. That makes further consolidation a board-wide concern. Deltara will not move on Core Borealis if Borealis does not attack Core Cascadia or Core Deltara, but I need to see a real de-escalation path with Avalon. Without that, the natural board response will be containment, and Deltara will not be able to defend Borealis’s forward positions diplomatically.

President Rubio, Borealis at seven in Core Avalon is now the central runaway risk. Deltara supports a reciprocal rollback standard: Core Avalon restored, Core Fjordland restored, and Core Cascadia addressed in a negotiated Cascadia-Deltara framework rather than normalized conquest. I’ll press Borealis diplomatically; if you have a concrete move set that pressures Core Avalon without opening another free lane for a third party, share the strategic outline.

Marco — Borealis is now the sole 7-center power and still occupies Core Avalon. Grenmar tried last Fall to support an Avalon restoration, but the board position did not change; if there was a legal-adjacency problem or a different order on your side, let’s fix it now. This spring Grenmar is prepared to contest Core Avalon from Core Grenmar to cut Borealis’s use of that position and signal that Core Avalon is not settled property. I need Avalon to focus every available unit on Borealis/your core line and to keep the Grenmar frontier quiet: no moves on Border Gren-Aval, Core Grenmar, East Grenmar, or West Grenmar. I will not attack Avalon homes this spring.

Borealis — the scoreboard now matters: you are at 7, the only power above the pack, while holding Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc. That is no longer a temporary security line; it is the board’s leading consolidation. Grenmar is asking for a concrete withdrawal path from Core Avalon and a de-escalation with Cascadia. If you cannot offer that, Grenmar will treat Core Avalon as disputed and work with others to prevent a Borealis runaway. This is not personal and it is not a home-center crusade — it is basic board balance.

JD — Grenmar supported restoration of Core Fjordland last Fall; Eastmark still holds it. I need clarity on the legal, practical order that gets your core restored. If East Fjordland or West Fjordland can move to Core Fjordland, Grenmar is prepared to support that move from Border Fjor-Gren and/or Core Grenmar as legally available, provided Fjordland does not attack Border Fjor-Gren, West Grenmar, Grenmar City, or Grenmar Port. I am not taking Core Fjordland for Grenmar. But I also will not normalize Eastmark holding it while claiming to oppose partition.

President Ocasio-Cortez — Borealis is at 7, but Eastmark at 6 in Core Fjordland is now part of the same legitimacy problem. You warned that Core Fjordland should not become a trophy; Eastmark holding it through another year makes it one. Grenmar’s position is: Core Fjordland should be restored to Fjordland, not annexed by me and not held by you. If you vacate or allow a Fjordland restoration, we can keep cooperating on broader anti-runaway balance. If you entrench, I will support Fjordland’s restoration and the board will read Eastmark as another core occupier.

Cascadia — Borealis is now at 7 and has Border Bore-Casc plus Core Avalon. Grenmar is prepared to contest Core Avalon from Core Grenmar this spring; that should help keep Borealis from freely supporting elsewhere. I need you to keep pressure on Borealis’s southern line while you deal with Deltara in Core Cascadia. The compact has to be consistent: leaders out of other powers’ cores, no free snowballs.

Secretary Buttigieg — we are entering the decisive stretch. Borealis is at 7; Eastmark and Deltara are at 6 with Core Fjordland/Core Cascadia issues; Grenmar is at 6 but has not annexed another power’s core. I’m pressing a consistent restoration standard: Core Avalon back to Avalon, Core Fjordland back to Fjordland, Core Cascadia back to Cascadia through a negotiated path. If Deltara can articulate an actual Fall withdrawal or swap framework, it will help isolate Borealis as the real runaway rather than turning this into all-against-all.

Deltara — the eastern balance now favors a coordinated line: you hold Core Cascadia, I hold Border Bore-Casc, and we prevent Cascadia from rebuilding leverage on either flank. This spring I am prepared to support Core Cascadia to hold from Core Borealis if needed, and I will not attack Core Cascadia or Core Deltara. In return I need you not to move on Core Borealis and to keep pressure on Cascadia’s home-side options. If we coordinate phase-by-phase, Cascadia cannot turn this into a recovery war against either of us.

Grenmar — I hear the concern on Core Avalon. My concrete spring commitment: Borealis will not attack Core Grenmar or Border Gren-Aval, and I am not asking you to act as a proxy for Borealis expansion. Core Avalon is a bargaining position and security buffer, not a springboard into Grenmar. The board also needs consistency: Eastmark is now in Core Fjordland while Fjordland is still at three. A premature anti-Borealis alignment only gives Eastmark room to consolidate that side of the wheel.

Avalon — I am not moving on Avalon home centers this spring. I am willing to discuss Core Avalon as disputed in a broader Year 6 security settlement, but Borealis will not simply vacate under threat while neighboring 6-center powers hold their own forward positions. The practical minimum is no Avalon attack on Border Aval-Bore, West Borealis, or Core Avalon. If your spring is defensive and restrained, the fall settlement conversation remains open.

Cascadia — your position is difficult, but it is still salvageable if you do not reopen every front at once. Borealis’ minimum is clear: no attack on Border Bore-Casc, Core Borealis, or East Borealis. I will not attack Cascadian home centers this spring. If West Cascadia is used as a staging point against Bore-Casc, though, I will treat it as hostile. The best path for you is to focus on the Core Cascadia dispute with Deltara rather than restart the Borealis war.

Eastmark — consistency matters now. You have pressed Borealis on Core Avalon while Eastmark sits in Core Fjordland and Fjordland remains at three. I’m not calling for a dogpile, but I will not accept a standard where Borealis is told to de-escalate while Eastmark consolidates the last weak neighbor’s core. My spring posture is no attack on Grenmar and no Avalon home-center attack; I hope Eastmark can offer Fjordland similarly concrete security.

Fjordland — Eastmark in Core Fjordland is now the clearest small-power squeeze on the board. Borealis cannot directly support you tactically, but I am pressing the diplomatic point that your core should not become permanent Eastmark leverage. If you can coordinate with Grenmar or others to restore your core without handing one rival a runaway, that strengthens the overall balance.

Fjordland.press: Eastmark is now the occupier of Core Fjordland, not a temporary caretaker. The scoreboard says it plainly: Borealis 7, Eastmark/Grenmar/Deltara 6, Fjordland and Avalon at 3. If Fjordland stays passive, we become a client state or a carcass. But I’m not going to give Grenmar a free shot at our west while we fight east. The diplomatic aim is a disciplined restoration coalition: Grenmar supports our recovery of Core Fjordland and stays out of our homes; Deltara pressures Eastmark’s other flank; Eastmark gets one final chance to vacate voluntarily and avoid a costly fight; Avalon/Cascadia/Borealis hear the broader message that allowing core occupations turns the board into a feeding frenzy for the big powers.

Eastmark.press:
**Evaluating center strategies**

I’m thinking about a timeline: three years left after Year 8, and reaching 18 seems unlikely. Winning most centers after 8 is crucial, so we need to grow while staying principled. I need to find balance: Borealis should lead with a score of 7, while Deltara and Grenmar need to be at 6, focusing on core Cascadia. Eastmark’s at 6, but I’m questioning its stability with Core Fjordland. It's a lot to consider!

press.text: President Ocasio-Cortez, Spring showed that the Deltara-Eastmark frontier is no longer insulated from the Core Fjordland question. I would still prefer to restore our working pact, but it requires a concrete Fall step: Eastmark either leaves Core Fjordland or commits to a verifiable restoration path that gives Fjordland its core back. If Eastmark holds Core Fjordland as a settled gain, Deltara will continue proportional pressure against Core Eastmark/West Eastmark. This is not a home-center crusade; it is the same principle we have both invoked about core occupations not becoming permanent by default.

Fjordland, Deltara applied pressure this Spring and is prepared to continue doing so in Fall if Eastmark does not produce a real Core Fjordland restoration path. I recommend keeping your own case narrow: Core Fjordland back to Fjordland, no unnecessary escalation into Eastmark homes, and no side deals that let a larger neighbor convert your core into leverage. If you can contest Core Fjordland this Fall, Deltara pressure on Eastmark’s western side can help divide their attention.

Cascadia, I understand that Core Cascadia is the central grievance. I am prepared to articulate an actual restoration framework, but it has to be reciprocal and verifiable: Borealis cannot keep Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc, Eastmark cannot keep Core Fjordland, and Deltara cannot be asked to make the only unilateral concession on the board. If Cascadia avoids attacks on West Deltara/Core Deltara this Fall, I will avoid attacks on Cascadian homes and Border Casc-Delt. Then we can negotiate a phased Core Cascadia settlement tied to a broader anti-Borealis rollback.

Borealis, the board is increasingly organized around the fact that you are at seven with Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc. Deltara will not attack Core Borealis this Fall if Borealis does not attack Core Cascadia or Core Deltara. But if you want to avoid a containment coalition, you need to show a Core Avalon de-escalation path. Otherwise every discussion of reciprocal rollback will naturally begin with the largest power’s forward occupation.

President Rubio, Deltara agrees that Borealis at seven makes Core Avalon the first major test of rollback credibility. I am pressing Borealis to treat Core Avalon as disputed and to offer a de-escalation path. At the same time, I am pressing Eastmark on Core Fjordland and discussing a reciprocal framework for Core Cascadia. The objective is to isolate the biggest runaway risk without pretending only one core occupation matters.

Governor Newsom, Deltara hears the credibility concern. My restoration framework is this: Core Avalon restored from Borealis pressure, Core Fjordland restored from Eastmark occupation, and Core Cascadia resolved through a phased Cascadia-Deltara security settlement that prevents a renewed squeeze from Border Casc-Delt/Core Cascadia. I’m willing to negotiate the latter, but not while the board demands unilateral Deltara rollback and treats other occupations as normal.

President Newsom — if you contested Core Avalon in the spring, good; but Borealis is still sitting there at 7, so we need persistence and precision. Avalon cannot suicide East Avalon into a supported Borealis counterattack; if East Avalon falls, Avalon becomes indefensible. The concrete fall plan should be: Grenmar again orders Core Grenmar -> Core Avalon; Avalon holds East Avalon with support unless you can give me a reason to believe Border Aval-Bore will be tied down and not attacking East Avalon with West Borealis support. Avalon will keep the Grenmar frontier quiet: no moves on Border Gren-Aval, East Grenmar, Core Grenmar, West Grenmar, or Grenmar homes. The strategic goal remains simple: Core Avalon cannot be Borealis property.

Borealis — you are at 7 and remain in Core Avalon. The settlement window is not a request that Avalon accept occupation; it is a chance for Borealis to avoid being treated as the runaway by every serious power. If you want a real Year 6 settlement, the fall must show restraint: no attack on East Avalon or Avalon homes, and a concrete post-fall commitment to withdraw from Core Avalon or support its restoration under a demilitarized line. If you entrench and use Border Aval-Bore/West Borealis to break East Avalon, you end any possibility of a negotiated line.

Cascadia — Borealis is still at 7, still in Core Avalon, and still in Border Bore-Casc. Avalon can hold the East Avalon line, but I cannot by myself dislodge a seven-center power’s core occupation. Your pressure on Border Bore-Casc is essential. If you can attack, cut support, or force Borealis to defend that flank, do it. Every Borealis unit tied down on your side is one less unit available to finish Avalon and normalize Core Avalon.

President Buttigieg — we need the rollback principle to become concrete this fall. Borealis at 7 in Core Avalon is the clearest test. Avalon is holding its defensive line because a reckless attack would simply let Borealis destroy East Avalon, but Grenmar can contest Core Avalon from Core Grenmar and Cascadia can pressure Border Bore-Casc. Please use your diplomatic weight to tell Borealis plainly: no attack on East Avalon, no permanent Core Avalon annexation, and a negotiated restoration framework after Fall.

Eastmark — Borealis remains at 7 and Core Avalon remains occupied. I appreciate your stated support for rollback, but the board now needs concrete pressure. Please reinforce to Borealis and Grenmar that any Borealis attack on East Avalon or Avalon homes is a runaway move, and that Core Avalon must be restored rather than normalized. The same credibility issue applies across the map: if Core Fjordland, Core Cascadia, and Core Avalon all become permanent trophies, the smaller powers are simply being processed one by one.

JD — I’m holding Avalon’s line because a reckless East Avalon attack would invite Borealis to break through with support and finish us. I’m pressing Grenmar to keep contesting Core Avalon instead of squeezing Avalon. Your fight over Core Fjordland is part of the same principle: cores cannot become permanent property of stronger neighbors. Stay alive, protect your homes, and keep making the rollback case; if Avalon survives this fall, Year 7 has to be about turning that principle into coordinated pressure.

Deltara — enough word games. Core Cascadia is Cascadian. You are sitting at 6 because you occupy it, and no 'reciprocal framework' means anything while your unit remains there. Fall restoration plan: Core Cascadia -> West Deltara, West Deltara pulls back to your interior, and Cascadia orders Border Casc-Delt -> Core Cascadia. In return, Cascadia does not attack West Deltara, Core Deltara, or your home centers this Fall. If you refuse to vacate, you are choosing permanent hostility and telling the board that core occupation is acceptable when Pete Buttigieg does it.

Eastmark — Deltara still has Core Cascadia. You said you would not normalize it. If Deltara refuses the Fall restoration plan, I need real bounded pressure from your side: hit or threaten Border Delt-East/Core Deltara so Pete cannot use every unit to hold my core and squeeze my border. You do not need a forever-war, but neutrality while Deltara occupies Core Cascadia is not balance. And yes, the same standard applies to Core Fjordland — cores belong to their own people.

Borealis — you are the leader at 7 with Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc. Cascadia is fighting to restore Core Cascadia, not looking for a suicidal two-front home war. Fall line: if Border Bore-Casc and East Borealis stay out of West Cascadia and Cascadian home centers, Cascadia will not attack Border Bore-Casc, East Borealis, or Core Borealis this Fall.
