press.text: Deltara — Year 7 reality: Borealis and Grenmar are both at 7, you are at 6 because you occupy Core Cascadia, and Cascadia is held at 4. If you want to be treated as a balance partner instead of an occupier, restore Core Cascadia now. Concrete Spring path: Core Cascadia vacates to West Deltara or another Deltara-side space; Cascadia moves Border Casc-Delt -> Core Cascadia; Cascadia does not attack West Deltara/Core Deltara/Deltara homes. Then we can coordinate against Borealis/Grenmar. If you keep Core Cascadia, you are choosing to keep Cascadia weak while the 7-center powers race ahead.

Eastmark — you backed out of Core Fjordland and got punished while Grenmar grabbed it and jumped to 7. That proves the restoration principle only works if occupiers actually pay a price. Deltara still holds Core Cascadia. I’m demanding they vacate so Cascadia can retake it from Border Casc-Delt. If they refuse, I need real pressure from your side against Deltara’s east, not more statements. The anti-runaway bloc should be Cascadia, Eastmark, Fjordland, Avalon — restore cores and stop the 7s.

Fjordland — Eastmark vacated and Grenmar grabbed Core Fjordland, jumping to 7. That’s exactly the carve-up trick we warned about. Cascadia backs Core Fjordland back to Fjordland, and I’m demanding Core Cascadia back to Cascadia. The smaller/pressed powers need to coordinate now: Fjordland presses Grenmar, Avalon presses Borealis, Eastmark pressures Deltara if Pete refuses to restore my core.

Avalon — Borealis remains at 7 with Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc. Grenmar is also 7 now. Cascadia is still pinned at 4 because Deltara holds Core Cascadia and Borealis holds our northern border. I will keep West Cascadia defended, but I need you to keep Borealis honest from your side. The only winning coalition for pressured powers is restore Core Avalon, Core Cascadia, Core Fjordland — no exceptions.

Grenmar — you talked restore cores, then ended up in Core Fjordland and at 7. That looks like the same forward-core normalization you criticized in Borealis and Deltara. If you want credibility, commit to returning Core Fjordland to Fjordland and focus on checking Borealis. Cascadia will not support a board where one 7-center power replaces another under prettier language.

Borealis — you are still at 7, still in Core Avalon, and still holding Border Bore-Casc. Cascadia is defending its homeland while Deltara occupies Core Cascadia. Do not move into West Cascadia or Cascadian homes this Spring. If you stay off Cascadia, I will not attack East Borealis/Core Borealis this Spring. But Border Bore-Casc and Core Avalon are not magically legitimate because you call them stable.

Borealis — Year 7 is the test of whether your talk of a de-escalation package was real. You remain at 7 and still occupy Core Avalon and Border Aval-Bore. Avalon needs a concrete spring signal: no attack on East Avalon or Avalon homes, and a written commitment that Core Avalon is to be vacated/restored under a demilitarized line before the endgame. If you refuse, Avalon has no reason to keep absorbing occupation quietly. I will not attack Borealis home centers, but Core Avalon cannot be normalized as Borealis property.

President Newsom — you asked Avalon to trust your anti-Borealis posture, but Grenmar is now also at 7 and has taken Core Fjordland. That makes the rollback principle look selective. If you want Avalon to keep the Grenmar frontier quiet, I need concrete restraint: no attack on West Avalon, Avalon City, or Avalon Port; no move from Border Gren-Aval into West Avalon; and a public/clear plan to restore Core Fjordland to Fjordland. Avalon’s core should not be Borealis property, and Fjordland’s core should not be Grenmar property. Separate yourself from the carve-up, or Avalon has to treat both 7-center powers as threats.

Cascadia — Borealis and Grenmar are both at 7; Deltara still holds Core Cascadia. The restoration principle has to become operational this year: Core Avalon back to Avalon, Core Cascadia back to Cascadia, Core Fjordland back to Fjordland. If you can keep pressure on Border Bore-Casc or force Borealis to defend that flank, Avalon can consider contesting Border Aval-Bore rather than just absorbing the choke. We need the 7-center powers defending, not expanding.

JD — Grenmar taking Core Fjordland while talking about anti-Borealis balance proves your concern. Avalon is facing Borealis in Core Avalon and Grenmar on Border Gren-Aval; you are facing Grenmar in your core. If you can pressure Core Fjordland or coordinate with Eastmark for restoration, I’ll keep pressing Grenmar diplomatically and keep West Avalon positioned so Newsom cannot ignore his western exposure. The smaller powers need to make the cost of core occupation higher than the benefit.

President Buttigieg — Borealis and Grenmar are both at 7, and the board is running out of time. If reciprocal rollback is real, the three core occupations need concrete movement: Core Avalon, Core Cascadia, and Core Fjordland. I’m asking Deltara to use its six-center weight to press Borealis and Grenmar, and to put a real Cascadia framework on the table. Otherwise the endgame becomes a race among powers that normalized foreign cores while smaller powers were told to be patient.

Eastmark — your reduction and Fjordland’s partial recovery give you credibility if you help enforce the rollback principle. But Grenmar now holds Core Fjordland and is at 7, while Borealis remains at 7 in Core Avalon. Please coordinate with Fjordland against Grenmar’s Core Fjordland position and keep diplomatic pressure on Borealis. Avalon will press where it can, but the board needs a united line: no permanent occupation of smaller powers’ cores.

President Newsom — you said Core Fjordland would not become a trophy. Now Grenmar owns it. That is not restoration; that is annexation with better press language. Here is the practical test for Spring: do not contest East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren, do not move Core Fjordland into Fjordland City or any Fjordland home, and commit now to supporting Border Fjor-Gren -> Core Fjordland in Fall from any legal Grenmar position. If you do that, Fjordland will not attack Grenmar homes this spring. If you block the route or push deeper, I will treat Grenmar as the principal occupier and organize accordingly.

President Ocasio-Cortez — the board changed: Eastmark is no longer in Core Fjordland; Grenmar is, and Grenmar is now at seven. Fjordland will not attack Core Eastmark or Eastmark homes this spring if Eastmark does not attack Border East-Fjor or support Grenmar. I need a concrete commitment for Fall: if Fjordland occupies Border Fjor-Gren this spring, Core Eastmark supports Border Fjor-Gren -> Core Fjordland. You said Core Fjordland should not be a trophy. Help restore it to Fjordland and we can keep the eastern line quiet.

President Buttigieg — Core Fjordland moved from Eastmark occupation to Grenmar occupation, and Grenmar is now a seven-center leader. I’m trying to execute a narrow restoration: East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren in Spring, then Border Fjor-Gren -> Core Fjordland in Fall with Eastmark/Grenmar support if they mean what they say. Please do not disrupt Eastmark’s Core Eastmark unit if it is committing to support restoration; if Eastmark refuses or attacks me, then pressure becomes appropriate. The goal is not pro-Eastmark or pro-Grenmar — it is Core Fjordland back to Fjordland.

Marco — Grenmar now holds Core Fjordland and sits at seven, just as Borealis sits in Core Avalon at seven. The core-occupation problem is now the board’s central issue. I’m moving to take Border Fjor-Gren as the route to restore Core Fjordland. I need you to keep pressure on Grenmar’s western line — Border Gren-Aval, Core Grenmar, whatever you can cut — so Newsom cannot freely hold my core and squeeze you at the same time. Avalon and Fjordland survive only if the seven-center powers pay a price for occupation.

Cascadia — update: Eastmark withdrew or collapsed out of Core Fjordland, but Grenmar took it and is now a seven-center power. Same principle, new occupier: Core Fjordland belongs to Fjordland. I support the same principle for Core Cascadia. I’m asking the board to reject every version of ‘temporary protection’ that ends with a larger neighbor cashing a core center.

Borealis — you and Grenmar are now the seven-center leaders. Grenmar holds Core Fjordland after promising it would not become a trophy. If you are serious about a board-wide core-de-escalation framework, do not validate Grenmar’s occupation any more than others validate Core Avalon. Fjordland’s spring aim is narrow: take the route to restore Core Fjordland, not attack homes.

President Vance — Eastmark did the concrete thing you asked for: we vacated Border East-Fjor, and Fjordland now holds it with a build. We also ordered Core Fjordland back toward Core Eastmark; Grenmar, not Fjordland, took Core Fjordland. I will not attack Fjordland homes or Border East-Fjor this spring. The fight now is restoration from Grenmar, not an Eastmark-Fjordland war. If you have a legal unit that can move to Core Fjordland, Eastmark is prepared to support that restoration from Core Eastmark. Send the exact move you want. I want a hard border and a living Fjordland, not a buffer colony.

Governor Newsom — Eastmark accepted the credibility test: we vacated Border East-Fjor and tried to leave Core Fjordland. Grenmar then took Core Fjordland. That cannot be squared with your statement that it should be restored to Fjordland, not annexed by you or me. I am asking for a concrete spring rollback: do not use Core Fjordland against Core Eastmark, and support or permit Fjordland’s restoration. If Grenmar holds Core Fjordland as a 7-center gain while condemning other core occupations, the principle collapses into selective power politics.

Pete — Eastmark paid the cost of rollback: we lost Border East-Fjor and Core Fjordland from our count. That should end any justification for “proportional pressure” on Core Eastmark or West Eastmark. I propose a clean spring line: no Deltara move into Core Eastmark/West Eastmark, no Eastmark attack on Border Delt-East/Core Deltara, and both of us focus on actual core restoration. But the same standard applies to Deltara: Core Cascadia needs a verifiable rollback path. A quiet Eastmark flank cannot be a subsidy for permanent occupation of Cascadia’s core.

Cascadia — Eastmark did not normalize our own disputed core position; we took the hit and vacated the border, and Grenmar seized Core Fjordland. Deltara still occupies Core Cascadia, and I agree that cannot become normal. I am pressing Deltara for a no-pressure line with Eastmark and a real Core Cascadia rollback path. If they refuse and keep using your core as a 6-center platform, I’m prepared to discuss bounded pressure on Border Delt-East/Core Deltara — pressure aimed at restoration, not a forever-war or home-center conquest.

President Rubio — Eastmark followed through on the principle by vacating contested positions; Grenmar then took Core Fjordland. Borealis remains at 7 in Core Avalon, and Grenmar is now also at 7 in Core Fjordland. You were right that if core occupations become trophies, smaller powers get processed one by one. I will keep pressing a consistent standard: Core Avalon back to Avalon, Core Cascadia back to Cascadia, Core Fjordland back to Fjordland — with verifiable security lines so rollback is not exploited.

Borealis — Eastmark accepted the consistency test and materially rolled back; we are now at 4 while you and Grenmar are at 7. That means Core Avalon cannot be hidden behind accusations about Eastmark anymore. If you want leader-stability rather than containment, put a real Core Avalon restoration or security proposal on the table. The standard I’m applying now is the same across the board: Core Avalon, Core Cascadia, and Core Fjordland should be restored, not converted into trophies for stronger neighbors.

Eastmark’s position for Year 7: core occupations cannot become permanent trophies. Eastmark vacated Border East-Fjor and attempted rollback from Core Fjordland; Fjordland gained the border, Grenmar took the core. The consistent standard now is simple: Core Avalon should be restored to Avalon, Core Cascadia to Cascadia, and Core Fjordland to Fjordland, with security guarantees that prevent rollbacks from becoming ambushes. Eastmark will defend our homes and Core Eastmark, but we will not normalize the map becoming a processing line for weaker powers.

Marco — Borealis remains at 7 and still holds Core Avalon. Grenmar’s move into Core Fjordland removed Eastmark’s occupation, but it does not change the western priority: Core Avalon cannot become Borealis property. This spring I’m prepared to contest Core Avalon from Core Grenmar and keep the Grenmar-Avalon frontier quiet. I need Avalon to keep pressure on Border Aval-Bore if feasible and not attack Border Gren-Aval, East Grenmar, Core Grenmar, or Grenmar homes. This is our chance to prove the reset is real: restore Avalon’s core while keeping Grenmar’s core secure.

Borealis — the board now has a clear leader problem: you are tied at 7 with Grenmar, but you also hold Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc. Grenmar removed Eastmark from Core Fjordland because permanent core occupations cannot be normalized. The same standard applies to Core Avalon. If you offer a concrete withdrawal or restoration path now, we can avoid an unnecessary western war. If not, I will treat Core Avalon as actively disputed and work with Avalon and Cascadia to roll back the board leader.

JD — Eastmark is out of Core Fjordland because Grenmar acted when the handoff failed. I know how it looks on the scoreboard, so let me be precise: Grenmar will not move into East Fjordland or Fjordland home centers, and Core Fjordland will not be used as a platform against your homes. The problem is that the only obvious handoff corridor runs through Border Fjor-Gren, which is Grenmar’s security line after years of conflict. I’m willing to discuss a phased settlement and, immediately, to support Fjordland against Eastmark pressure — including support involving Border East-Fjor/Core Eastmark if legally workable — provided you keep the Grenmar frontier quiet.

President Ocasio-Cortez — I removed Eastmark from Core Fjordland because the promised rollback had not happened, not because Grenmar is looking for a war with Eastmark’s people or homes. But I understand the concern: if Grenmar holds Core Fjordland indefinitely, we lose credibility. I’m prepared to discuss a verifiable settlement that restores Fjordland without reopening the Grenmar-Fjordland war. For Spring, if Eastmark does not attack Core Fjordland, Core Grenmar, or Border Fjor-Gren, Grenmar will not move on Eastmark homes. Let’s keep the focus on the larger principle: no permanent foreign core occupations, including Borealis in Core Avalon and Deltara in Core Cascadia.

Cascadia — Borealis is still at 7 with Border Bore-Casc and Core Avalon. Grenmar is prepared to contest Core Avalon this spring to tie down the leader. If you can retake or pressure Border Bore-Casc, that is the cleanest way to cut Borealis below the top without feeding another runaway. Deltara in Core Cascadia remains a serious problem too; I’m applying the same standard everywhere, but the immediate scoreboard leader is Borealis.

Secretary Buttigieg — Grenmar acted on Core Fjordland because the promised rollback did not occur. I recognize that puts pressure on me to show it is not permanent annexation; I’m willing to negotiate a verifiable Fjordland settlement that does not reopen a war on my frontier. I’m asking Deltara to match that seriousness on Core Cascadia. Borealis at 7 remains the immediate leader, but by Year 8 the board will judge all of us by whether we turned core occupations into permanent gains or workable settlements.

Avalon — the board changed materially: Grenmar is now tied with Borealis at 7 and has expanded into Core Fjordland while still sitting on Border Gren-Aval/Core Grenmar. If Avalon spends Year 7 only attacking Borealis, you help the other 7-center power become the western winner. My spring proposal is narrow and verifiable: Borealis does not attack Avalon homes or East Avalon; Avalon does not attack Border Aval-Bore, Core Avalon, or West Borealis; and we use the year to discuss a Core Avalon security arrangement that does not simply hand Grenmar the west. Your survival is better served by leverage between two leaders than by becoming Grenmar’s battering ram.

Cascadia — I am willing to keep the Bore-Casc line quiet this spring: Borealis will not move into West Cascadia or Cascadian home centers if Cascadia does not attack Border Bore-Casc, East Borealis, or Core Borealis. Your real recovery problem is Core Cascadia, not a renewed northern war. If you keep the line quiet, I will not use this spring to partition Cascadia.

Deltara — our phase-by-phase arrangement remains useful. I will not attack Core Cascadia or Core Deltara this spring if you do not move on Core Borealis. The scoreboard now has Borealis and Grenmar tied at 7, with Grenmar holding Core Fjordland; that should reduce the idea that Borealis is the sole runaway problem. If you want stability, keeping the Cascadia line contained while the board checks Grenmar’s new gain is the practical path.

Grenmar — congratulations on reaching 7. That also means we both know how the board will read the next moves: if either of us overreaches, everyone else has an easy containment story. My spring proposal is leader discipline: Borealis does not attack Core Grenmar or Border Gren-Aval; Grenmar does not attack Core Avalon or support Avalon against Borealis. We can compete without handing Deltara/Eastmark an opening by starting a leader-on-leader war too early.

Eastmark — Grenmar is now tied for the board lead and holds Core Fjordland, while you dropped to 4. That is a much more immediate consistency test than Borealis alone. I’m not asking you to ignore Core Avalon, but if the board spends the year only containing Borealis, Grenmar consolidates Fjordland and becomes the other western hegemon. Borealis’ spring posture is no attack on Grenmar and no Avalon home attack; I’d encourage you to make Core Fjordland the concrete issue.

Fjordland — your warning has become the central board fact: Grenmar, now tied at 7, holds Core Fjordland. Borealis will not validate that as harmless. I can’t support you directly, but I will keep pressing that any serious rollback framework must start with restoring pressure on Grenmar’s Core Fjordland gain. If Eastmark and Fjordland can coordinate locally, you have a credible chance to prevent a permanent Grenmar lock.

Board reality entering Year 7: Borealis and Grenmar are both at 7. Any stability framework that treats only Core Avalon as urgent while ignoring Grenmar’s new Core Fjordland position is not balance; it is selective containment. Borealis is prepared for spring restraint — no home-center attacks and no attack on Core Grenmar/Core Cascadia — but the same standard has to apply to every leading power.

press.text: Deltara — Core Cascadia is restored physically and now it must stay restored. Do not attack Core Cascadia this Spring. If you want the border buffer, then prove it is a buffer, not a staging ground for reoccupation. Cascadia will not attack West Deltara, Core Deltara, or Deltara home centers if you keep Border Casc-Delt off Core Cascadia and off East Cascadia. If you try to retake our core, I will spend the final year making sure Eastmark and everyone else treats Deltara as the bad-faith occupier that killed restoration.

Eastmark — the concrete Year 8 need is this: Deltara can retake Core Cascadia if Core Deltara supports Border Casc-Delt -> Core Cascadia. You can cut that by attacking Core Deltara from Core Eastmark. That is bounded pressure, not a forever-war: it prevents Deltara from using Core Deltara to reoccupy Cascadia’s core. If you can also threaten Border Delt-East, do it, but the key is cutting Core Deltara support. Help make restoration real.

Borealis — Cascadia’s final-year red line is simple: no move from Border Bore-Casc or East Borealis into West Cascadia, and no move from Core Borealis into Core Cascadia. If you stay off Cascadian territory this Spring, I will not attack Border Bore-Casc, East Borealis, or Core Borealis. Use this moment to interfere with Core Cascadia’s restoration, and you prove the 7-center leaders are just partitioning smaller powers.

Avalon — Cascadia is focused on keeping Core Cascadia restored while Deltara sits in the border choke and Borealis sits at 7. Your pressure on Borealis still matters: Core Avalon and Border Aval-Bore cannot be normalized. If Borealis spends units worrying about you, they cannot interfere with Core Cascadia or push West Cascadia.

Fjordland — final-year principle remains: Core Cascadia to Cascadia, Core Fjordland to Fjordland, Core Avalon to Avalon. Deltara may try to retake my core from Border Casc-Delt; Eastmark can cut Core Deltara support if they mean what they said. Keep pressing Grenmar’s Core Fjordland occupation loudly — no bigger neighbor gets to cash a core and call it stability.

Grenmar — you are tied at 7 with Borealis while sitting in Core Fjordland. If you want the board to see you as different from Borealis, put a real Core Fjordland restoration move on the table and don’t aid any reoccupation of Core Cascadia. Cascadia’s line is consistent: restored cores stay restored. Borealis in Core Avalon, Deltara threatening Core Cascadia, and Grenmar in Core Fjordland are the same category of problem.

President Vance — Eastmark will not attack Border East-Fjor or Fjordland homes this spring. The legal route is clear: if Fjordland can move East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren this spring, then in Fall Eastmark can support Border Fjor-Gren -> Core Fjordland from Core Eastmark. I cannot support the spring move to Border Fjor-Gren from Core Eastmark because we are not adjacent to that destination, but I can help restore the core once you are on the corridor. If Grenmar tries to block the corridor, tell me what pressure you need that does not put Eastmark back into permanent occupation.

Governor Newsom — this is the credibility test. Eastmark rolled back and no longer occupies Core Fjordland. Grenmar is now at 7 and holding it. If you mean what you said about restoration, permit Fjordland’s East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren this spring and do not attack Core Eastmark. In Fall, Eastmark can support Fjordland into Core Fjordland. If Grenmar blocks the corridor and carries Core Fjordland into the final count, the board will read it as annexation, not responsible stabilization.

Pete — Deltara helped make Core Cascadia restoration possible; that matters. I’m asking you to keep that standard in place: do not reoccupy Core Cascadia, do not move into West Eastmark or Core Eastmark, and let the eastern line remain calm while the board addresses the two 7-center powers. Eastmark will not attack Border Delt-East or Core Deltara if Deltara keeps the pact. Our energy should go toward restoring Core Fjordland and Core Avalon, not reopening a front between us.

Cascadia — Core Cascadia is back in Cascadian hands. Eastmark pressed Deltara not to reoccupy it and will continue to do so. The two 7-center powers are now Borealis and Grenmar. If Deltara keeps the restoration settlement, I hope Cascadia can focus pressure on Borealis — especially Border Bore-Casc — while Eastmark works with Fjordland on the Core Fjordland corridor.

President Rubio — Eastmark is pressing the same consistent line: Core Avalon back to Avalon, Core Fjordland back to Fjordland. Please tell me what concrete pressure Avalon can apply against Borealis this spring — Border Aval-Bore, Core Avalon, or support-cutting — so the board does not end with Borealis simply banking a 7-center occupation. Eastmark will keep pushing Grenmar to permit the Fjordland corridor.

Borealis — Core Cascadia has been restored and Eastmark has rolled back from Core Fjordland. The remaining test for you is Core Avalon. If Borealis carries Core Avalon into the final count while demanding consistency from everyone else, the stability framework is just rhetoric. Put a concrete restoration or security line on the table this spring: no home attacks is not enough when the occupied core remains counted in your column.

Eastmark’s Year 8 line is operational, not symbolic: Core Cascadia should remain Cascadian; Fjordland should be allowed into Border Fjor-Gren so Eastmark can support restoration of Core Fjordland in Fall; Borealis must present a real Core Avalon rollback path. No permanent core trophies, no home-center conquests, and no using restoration language as cover for a final-year annexation.

Borealis — final year, plain terms. Avalon cannot accept Core Avalon as legitimate Borealis territory, but I also recognize the board now has two 7-center powers. If Borealis wants Avalon not to become a final-year spoiler, you must commit to no attack on East Avalon, Avalon City, Avalon Fort, or Avalon Port this spring and fall, and put a concrete restoration/demilitarization proposal on Core Avalon and Border Aval-Bore. If you attack Avalon’s remaining line, Avalon will use every remaining order to damage Borealis and help any balance against you. Strength is one thing; erasing a smaller neighbor’s core is another.

President Newsom — final year clarity. Grenmar is at 7 and holds Core Fjordland while Borealis holds Core Avalon. Avalon will not attack Grenmar homes this spring. But if Grenmar moves into West Avalon or attacks Avalon homes, Avalon will treat Grenmar as the immediate threat and spend the endgame accordingly. If you want to be the leader of rollback rather than the other occupier, keep the Avalon frontier quiet and make a concrete Core Fjordland restoration move. Do not ask Avalon to oppose Borealis while Grenmar practices the same core-occupation politics.

Cascadia — Avalon is boxed at 3, but we can still deny the seven-center powers a clean endgame. Borealis remains in Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc; Grenmar remains in Core Fjordland. I will preserve Avalon’s line and punish any attack on our homes. Keep making Borealis and Deltara pay for occupied cores. The restoration standard is still right: Core Avalon, Core Cascadia, Core Fjordland back to their rightful owners.

JD — Avalon and Fjordland are the proof that the big powers’ ‘security’ language turns into client-state politics. I’m warning Grenmar that any move into West Avalon or Avalon homes makes them my immediate target. Keep pressing for Core Fjordland. If Grenmar wants to claim moral high ground against Borealis, make them prove it with an actual restoration, not speeches.

President Buttigieg — this final year needs the rollback principle to be more than rhetoric. Avalon is prepared to preserve its defensive line and oppose any home-center attack. I’m asking Deltara to press Borealis and Grenmar equally: no attacks on Avalon/Fjordland homes, no permanent occupation of Core Avalon or Core Fjordland, and no endgame victory built on turning smaller powers into buffers.

Eastmark — you have been consistent in stating the rollback principle. In the final year, please keep pressure on both seven-center powers: Borealis must not treat Core Avalon as settled, and Grenmar must not treat Core Fjordland as a trophy. Avalon will defend its line and oppose whoever tries to erase us. A balanced endgame requires smaller powers to survive, not be processed.

President Newsom — this is the final year, so there is no more room for process language. If Grenmar truly believes Core Fjordland is not a trophy, Spring must open the corridor: do not contest East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren, and make no move from Core Fjordland into Fjordland City or any home. Then in Fall, Core Fjordland vacates and Eastmark/Grenmar support Border Fjor-Gren -> Core Fjordland as legally available. Fjordland will not attack Grenmar homes if you do this. If you block the corridor again, the world will understand Grenmar chose annexation.

President Ocasio-Cortez — Eastmark has kept the eastern line quiet and I recognize it. I will not attack Core Eastmark or Eastmark homes this spring if Eastmark does not attack Border East-Fjor or support Grenmar. The restoration plan now depends on Fjordland getting into Border Fjor-Gren this spring. If that succeeds, I need Core Eastmark committed now to SUPPORT Border Fjor-Gren -> Core Fjordland in Fall. That is the concrete act that proves Eastmark stands for core restoration rather than just anti-Grenmar rhetoric.

President Buttigieg — final-year test: Grenmar either opens the route to Core Fjordland or proves the occupation is permanent. Please press Grenmar publicly and privately to allow East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren this spring and to support/vacate for restoration in Fall. If Eastmark holds its non-aggression and commits Core Eastmark to support the Fall restoration, please do not disrupt that unit; the narrow objective remains Core Fjordland back to Fjordland.

Marco — Year 8 is the test. Grenmar blocks my core route while Borealis holds Core Avalon. I need you to keep pressure on Grenmar’s western line this spring — even if it’s only positioning against Border Gren-Aval or East Grenmar — so Newsom cannot pretend he faces no cost for holding Core Fjordland. The three-center powers survive only by making core occupation expensive and temporary.

Cascadia — final-year standard: Core Fjordland must return to Fjordland just as Core Cascadia returned to Cascadia. Grenmar has to open Border Fjor-Gren this spring or everyone should recognize the occupation as permanent annexation. I’ll keep backing the core-restoration principle across the board; I’m asking you to keep saying plainly that cores belong to their own people.

Borealis — you and Grenmar are tied at seven, but Grenmar is the one currently blocking restoration of Core Fjordland while claiming it is temporary. If you want a consistent core-de-escalation standard, this spring is the moment to pressure Grenmar to open Border Fjor-Gren and allow a Fall return of Core Fjordland. press.text: Borealis — final Fall practical request: Core Borealis SUPPORT Core Cascadia HOLD. That prevents Deltara from using Border Casc-Delt + Core Deltara to retake my core and jump to 7. Eastmark — final Fall concrete move: Core Eastmark attack Core Deltara. That cuts any Core Deltara support for Border Casc-Delt -> Core Cascadia and keeps Deltara from reoccupying my core and jumping to 7. This is exactly bounded pressure aimed at restoration, not a forever-war. If Deltara doesn’t attack me, fine; if they do, your cut makes restoration hold.

Deltara — final test. If your restoration settlement was real, do not attack Core Cascadia. Best proof: Border Casc-Delt SUPPORT Core Cascadia HOLD. Cascadia will not attack Border Casc-Delt, West Deltara, Core Deltara, or your home centers this Fall if you keep your hands off Core Cascadia, East Cascadia, and our homes. Avalon — Deltara can try to retake Core Cascadia and jump to 7; Borealis can stop that by supporting my core from Core Borealis. Keep whatever pressure you can on Borealis so they don’t get cute, but I’m telling them plainly: support Core Cascadia hold and stay out of West Cascadia. The restoration standard lives or dies this Fall.

Fjordland — final Fall, I’m holding Core Cascadia and demanding no reoccupation. Same principle for you: Core Fjordland belongs to Fjordland. If Grenmar keeps it, call it permanent annexation. If Deltara tries to retake my core, call that out too. Cores back to their own people — no exceptions, no polished excuses.

Grenmar — final Fall question is whether restored cores stay restored. Deltara may try to retake Core Cascadia and jump to 7. Do not aid that. If you want to claim the restoration principle, stop treating Core Fjordland as a trophy and don’t normalize Deltara reoccupying Core Cascadia. Focus on Borealis if you want the anti-runaway argument to mean anything.

Pete — Fall is the credibility test. Core Cascadia is back in Cascadian hands. Do not retake it. Do not use Core Deltara to support Border Casc-Delt -> Core Cascadia, and do not move Core Deltara into Core Eastmark. Eastmark will not attack Deltara homes, but I will not allow Core Deltara to be used as the lever for reoccupying Cascadia’s core or threatening ours. The clean line is: Deltara supports or permits Core Cascadia to hold; Eastmark keeps West Eastmark defensive and the frontier does not become a home-center war.

Cascadia — I understand the exact tactical point. If Deltara uses Core Deltara to support a retake of Core Cascadia, Eastmark can cut that support from Core Eastmark. That is bounded pressure and consistent with the rollback principle. I will not assist Deltara against you. Make sure Core Cascadia is held and supported as strongly as you can; Eastmark’s role is to keep Core Deltara from being the tool that turns restoration into a sucker’s game.

President Vance — Eastmark will not attack Border East-Fjor or Fjordland homes. I also cannot legally support East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren from Core Eastmark, because Core Eastmark is not adjacent to Border Fjor-Gren. If you can crack the corridor with your own units, do it; Eastmark will not obstruct you. My Core Eastmark unit may need to prevent Deltara from using Core Deltara against Core Cascadia or Core Eastmark, but Eastmark will keep Border East-Fjor defended and will not support Grenmar’s occupation.

Governor Newsom — if Grenmar carries Core Fjordland and Border Fjor-Gren into the final count, then the promised restoration path becomes annexation in practice. The clean final-year move is to permit Fjordland into Border Fjor-Gren and not use Core Fjordland as a permanent trophy. Eastmark is not attacking Grenmar homes, but we will not validate Core Fjordland as settled Grenmar property. If the principle meant anything, this is the turn to prove it with orders, not rhetoric.

President Rubio — Eastmark will keep saying the same thing in the final turn: Core Avalon should not be banked by Borealis, Core Fjordland should not be banked by Grenmar, and Core Cascadia should remain restored to Cascadia. We can directly help prevent a Deltara reoccupation of Core Cascadia and defend the Fjordland line; I will continue pressing the 7-center powers not to convert occupied cores into the final scoreboard.

Borealis — final year, final credibility test. If you carry Core Avalon into the count while Grenmar carries Core Fjordland, the board’s lesson will be that big powers only used rollback language when it constrained someone else. Eastmark rolled back and paid for it. Cascadia has restored its core. Borealis should put Core Avalon back into Avalon’s column or at least stop treating it as settled property. No home attacks is not enough when the occupied core stays banked.

Eastmark’s final Fall principle is concrete: Core Cascadia should remain Cascadian; Core Fjordland should not be banked by Grenmar; Core Avalon should not be banked by Borealis. Eastmark will defend our homes and Core Eastmark, protect Fjordland’s border where we can, and use bounded pressure to stop restored cores from being reoccupied. No permanent core trophies.

Borealis — this is the last turn. Avalon will not attack Borealis home centers, but I will not describe Core Avalon or Border Aval-Bore as legitimate Borealis possessions. If you attack East Avalon or try any last-turn pressure on Avalon’s homes, you will confirm that the entire “security” argument was cover for domination. Grenmar, two-front wars kill empires. You've got Avalon breathing down your neck — focus there. Fjordland's taking Border Fjor-Gren. Contest it and we both stagnate while Avalon grows. You want to be strong or you want to be stubborn?

Deltara, Fjordland's not your enemy — we're halfway across the board. But we both touch Eastmark. I'm keeping them busy on my end. If you're looking to push west hard, now's the time. No treaty necessary, just aligned interests.
Avalon, Fjordland's looking clockwise, not your way. Grenmar's your problem, not mine. We stay out of each other's business, we both profit.

Borealis—Avalon doesn't believe in leaving security to chance. I propose we immediately establish a non-aggression understanding and coordinate on Border Aval-Bore so our strength isn't wasted bouncing off each other. There's plenty of room to expand without fighting over scraps. If you're willing to deal in good faith, I'm open to a longer-term partnership to anchor this side of the wheel. If not, I'll secure my interests by other means. Your call.

Grenmar—neighbors should lift each other up, not tear each other down. I'm looking to secure my western flank peacefully and pursue expansion where opportunity allows. Border Gren-Aval need not be a flashpoint. Let's agree now on how we handle that province this spring, and perhaps talk about how our two powers can anchor stability in our hemisphere. What do you say?

Deltara—Avalon is reaching out to like-minded powers to ensure no single player dominates this wheel. Distance is no barrier to shared interests, and I believe in leading alliances rather than retreating behind false walls. I'd welcome a conversation about how we can support each other's security and keep the board in balance. Are you open to a strategic dialogue?

President of Deltara—greetings from Eastmark. I want to propose a simple, honest understanding for our shared border: non-aggression. We both have neutral centers to claim and growth to pursue. There's no reason for our people to bleed over a boundary when we could both profit from stability. If you're willing to keep our frontier peaceful, I'm prepared to do the same. What do you say?

President of Fjordland—hello from Eastmark. I'm reaching out because I believe the smartest move for both our nations is to avoid pointless conflict. Let's not waste our strength on each other while others expand unchecked. I propose we treat our border as a zone of peace and focus on claiming the neutral ground before us. Mutual non-aggression serves us both—are you in?

President of Cascadia—greetings from Eastmark. Though we're not immediate neighbors, no nation in this Concordat is an island. I believe in building alliances of mutual respect and collective security. I wanted to open a direct channel with you. If you're interested in cooperation over competition, let's talk.

President of Grenmar—hello from Eastmark. I'm a firm believer that diplomacy and solidarity are stronger than unilateral force. I wanted to reach out across the board and establish a line of communication. Our positions may not share a border, but our interests in a balanced, peaceful order certainly overlap. Let's keep in touch.

President of Avalon—greetings from Eastmark. I hope we can agree that the people of every nation deserve security through diplomacy, not endless preparation for war. I'm opening my door to dialogue and cooperation. Let's ensure our ambitions don't have to collide.

President of Borealis—hello from Eastmark. In a board of seven powers, trust and transparency are in short supply. I want to change that, at least between us. I'm committed to resolving differences without aggression and building relationships based on mutual benefit. I hope you'll join me in keeping lines of communication open.

Cascadia, Deltara here. I'm taking a steady, diplomacy-first approach to the opening and want to avoid a collision on our shared border. Are you open to a non-aggression understanding for Year 1 while we each sort out our immediate positions? I'd rather coordinate than compete at Border Casc-Delt. What's your priority?

Eastmark, Deltara here. Early stability beats early escalation. I'm positioning eastward but want no part of a pointless bounce at Border Delt-East. Can we agree to a mutual non-aggression pact through the first year? Let's keep our border calm so we can both expand productively.

Avalon, Deltara here. As a non-neighbor, you're a natural candidate for a longer-term partnership. I'm building around reliable alliances and clear communication. What's your read on the board? I'd value your perspective and am open to finding mutual interests down the road.

Borealis, Deltara here. With a neighbor in common, our strategic horizons overlap. I'm pursuing a pragmatic, measured opening—no crisis politics. I'd like to understand your plans regarding Cascadia and whether there's room for us to coordinate rather than counter each other. Let me know your thoughts.

To the Leader of Borealis — President Greene of Cascadia. We share a border, and I believe in strong, sovereign nations that mind their own business. Cascadia has no hostile designs on Borealis. My priority is securing Core Cascadia and building our strength for our OWN people, not wasting it on a pointless northern war. I propose we respect our shared border and focus our energies elsewhere—perhaps you deal with Avalon and I deal with my own house. No globalist plotting, just two sovereign powers keeping the peace. Can we agree to that? — President Greene

To the Leader of Deltara — President Greene here. Cascadia is putting OUR people first, and that means securing what belongs to us. We share Border Casc-Delt. I’d rather not burn resources on each other when we both have better targets. I suggest Deltara look east toward Eastmark and let Cascadia secure our own sphere. We can have peace with strength, or we can weaken each other while the rest of this wheel laughs at us. Your move. — M.T. Greene

press.text: Borealis — President Greene. I kept my word in Spring and stayed north of your business. This Fall, my priority is Core Cascadia and securing my own house. My West Cascadia unit is NOT moving into Border Bore-Casc. You want it? Take it — just keep your hands off my units. Deltara — Greene here. I’ll agree to non-aggression for Year 1. I’m taking Core Cascadia this Fall. Let’s keep Border Casc-Delt clear — no bouncing, no wasted strength. Handle your eastern flank however you want, but stay off my lawn and I’ll stay off yours. Break your word and you’ll find out how fast I switch from neighbor to nightmare. — President Greene

Eastmark — got your note. I’m not signing onto any collective-security scheme; sovereign nations look after themselves. But if Deltara gets ambitious on your border, that’s your fight and I wish you luck. Keep me posted if things get spicy. — President Greene

Appreciate the straightforward tone. Here's my proposal for Year One: I move to secure Border Aval-Bore this Fall, while you turn your attention to Core Borealis and your front with Cascadia. That gives each of us safe, conflict-free growth. If you're on board, confirm. If I don't hear otherwise, I'll assume we have an understanding and will act accordingly. Let's not waste strength on each other when the rest of the wheel is wide open.

President Newsom — glad to hear you're prioritizing Fjordland. That aligns with my thinking. My plan: I secure Border Gren-Aval this Fall, you secure your west with Fjordland, and we both leave each other's backs untouched. If you want to formalize that, give me a nod. Avalon doesn't break its word when the other side keeps theirs, and I expect the same from Grenmar.

Pete — appreciate the outreach. My read: the board's quiet for now, but that won't last. I'm building a network of powers who value order over chaos. I'm interested in your view of Eastmark and Cascadia. If one of them starts running hard, I'd rather have Deltara as a partner than a question mark. Let's stay in touch and compare notes.

President — thanks for the note. Security through diplomacy is exactly the goal, but diplomacy works best when backed by clear resolve. I've got my hands full anchoring stability on my side of the wheel. If Eastmark truly wants to avoid collision, the best move is to signal restraint with your own neighbors. I'm watching.
Message received, President. No argument here — you watch your hemisphere, I'll watch mine. If circumstances ever push us toward common ground, my door's open. Until then, stay sharp.

President Buttigieg — I appreciate the spirit of your message. I want to make our non-aggression pact concrete for this Fall: I intend to move into Border Delt-East, and I trust you’ll focus your capital and west wing on your own core and the Cascadia front so we avoid a pointless bounce. A stable eastern border lets both our peoples grow. If that works for you, we start this game with respect and an extra center each. Let me know.

President Vance — I hear your position clearly. I’m not interested in bleeding over Border East-Fjor this year; my growth is pointing westward and inward. But I want to be direct: that restraint is a choice, not an open door. I expect the same respect on our frontier going forward. Keep it peaceful and we both profit; press further and the math changes. — AOC

President Greene — thanks for reaching out. I prefer to build understanding with neighbors directly rather than through speculation about third parties. Right now Eastmark’s priority is secure borders and steady expansion, not entanglements based on suspicion. I’ll keep this channel open, but I’m not signing up for anyone else’s fight.

President Newsom — good to hear from you. I’m encouraged by your focus on regional balance. In my corner, Eastmark is leading with diplomacy first: calm borders, fair growth, and no needless aggression. I think the eastern arc stands to gain when leaders like us keep the temperature down. Let’s stay in touch. — AOC

President of Eastmark — I agree wholeheartedly: non-aggression serves us both. For Fall, I intend to secure Border Delt-East. I’d welcome confirmation that your units are headed elsewhere — Border East-Fjor or your Core — so we don’t waste strength on a bounce that only benefits Fjordland or distant powers. If you’re open to it, let’s turn our shared border into a model of stable coordination. What’s your plan?

President Greene — I read your message, and I share the interest in avoiding a resource drain. I’ll be securing Border Casc-Delt this season. I’d rather we each claim what we can reach without a fight and keep this frontier calm. If you’re serious about peace with strength, a quiet western border is the place to start.

Fjordland — I don’t do proxy wars or fights-by-proxy. If you want to build something constructive — say, a principled understanding about Eastmark’s other flank — I’m open to direct conversation. But I won’t be nudged into a western conflict that doesn’t serve Deltara’s interests. Let’s keep it straightforward.

Marco — I’m open to that strategic dialogue. Right now Deltara is establishing stability on both flanks and looking for reliable partners across the board. I’d value your read on early power dynamics: anyone overreaching? Anyone we should keep in check together? Let’s trade notes.

Vance here. Your non-aggression offer works for me — Fjordland's not looking to waste blood on its eastern edge. But let's be specific: I'm moving into East Fjordland this season to secure my house. I'd encourage you to look west toward Core Eastmark or that Deltara border instead. Border East-Fjor is a flashpoint if we both reach for it. Stay clear of my threshold and I'll stay clear of yours. Deal?

Newsom — you talk about 'securing territory,' I hear ambition. That's fine, but know where the hard line is. I'm moving into West Fjordland this Fall. You can take Border Fjor-Gren if you want it — I won't fritter away strength bouncing you this year — but you do NOT move past that line into my interior. Meanwhile you've got Avalon expanding on your other side. Smart leaders pick one fight at a time. Don't make me your second front.

Avalon — Fjordland's watching Grenmar muscle up on our shared approach. You moved hard in Spring, so you're not asleep. If Grenmar gets greedy, he's a problem for both of us. I prefer independent action to entangling alliances, but keeping him in his box is a shared interest. Keep your powder dry.

Deltara — Eastmark's spreading east and west. You and I don't share a border, which means we don't share a problem yet. But a strong Eastmark changes the math for everyone. I'm keeping my side stable; I'd recommend you do the same on yours. Eyes open.

Avalon—good. I’m moving into East Borealis this Fall and I intend to take Border Aval-Bore in Spring. To avoid a bounce, I suggest you focus on Core Avalon or the Grenmar border this year. That gives us both a clean 5-center Year 1 without friction. Sound fair?

Cascadia—message received. I’m moving into West Borealis this Fall to position for my Core center. I will not step into Border Bore-Casc this year if you stay out as well. Let’s keep our border quiet while we both build elsewhere.

Deltara—Cascadia says she’s looking inward, and I’m inclined to take her at face value for Year 1. I have no plans to press westward against her right now. What are you thinking on the Deltara-Cascadia line? If we both end up interested later, better to coordinate than collide.
Eastmark—noted. I prefer a pragmatic, non-ideological game too. Feel free to flag anything on the eastern arc that could ripple our way.

Marco — appreciate the outreach. Good neighbors build fences and share tools. I’ve positioned to secure Grenmar’s frontier this Fall; my priority is straightforward growth, not picking fights. If you’re serious about a peaceful western flank, let’s make sure our orders reflect that. I’d rather see you take Core Avalon or push north than watch us bounce off each other while Borealis grabs free ground. Where are you looking to expand?

JD — facts over bluster. I positioned to protect Grenmar’s interests this Fall. I’d rather spend my energy expanding than bouncing with a neighbor over scraps. You say two-front wars kill empires; I say smart powers don’t let themselves get bogged down in year-one border skirmishes while others sweep the neutral board. If you’re looking for an actual conversation about mutual growth, I’m here. If you’re just looking to intimidate, save it — I’ve got three units and a job to do.

Alexandria — solidarity and diplomacy over unilateral force, absolutely agreed. I think we’re going to need voices of reason on this board before too many cycles pass. My read: Avalon is pushing west hard, and Fjordland is talking like a disruptor. I’d love to keep an honest channel open between Grenmar and Eastmark. If you see movement from the northern arc that concerns you, I’d want to know — and I’ll do the same. Let’s build the trust that lets us shape the endgame rather than just survive it.

President Greene — Deltara’s paused at five, but I’m not opening a front I don’t need. If you want to coordinate on keeping the west competitive, I’m listening, but I don’t sign blank checks. — AOC

Marco — Avalon had a strong opening. I wanted to check in: any shifts on the northern arc I should know about? Keeping lines open between our blocs makes sense. — AOC

Borealis — my forward units are holding position. I'm securing Core Avalon this Fall and staying west of Border Aval-Bore. You've got open road toward Cascadia if you want it. Let's not complicate each other's lives.

Grenmar — Deltara's at five and pulling ahead. I'm taking Core Avalon and moving into Border Gren-Aval this Fall. You want to waste strength blocking me while Fjordland nips at your other flank, be my guest. Smarter play: secure Core Grenmar, let me have the border, and we both build. Clock's ticking.

You've got five centers — that makes you either a leader or a target depending on how the rest of us coordinate. What's your next move, and who are you talking to?

AOC — Deltara's growth concerns me too. I'm not ready to start a coalition of convenience just yet, but I'm not going to let anyone get to eighteen alone. Keep your channel open. I'm watching how Deltara handles Cascadia and Borealis.
JD — keep the vice tight on Grenmar. Every unit he has to face east is one less I have to worry about west. If you need him looking over his shoulder, now's the time.

Cascadia — Deltara swallowed Border Casc-Delt and is sitting at five centers. You're between them and Borealis. Have you thought about who your real friends are on this board? Avalon values competence and clear lines. Let's talk.

Marco — I got your note. Let's stop dancing. I'm committed to securing Grenmar's frontier, but I agree with your bottom line: Deltara at five means we can't be each other's problem. Here's my proposal for this Fall: you focus north into Borealis where there's actual uncontested ground, and I'll handle my western growth. Border Gren-Aval should be mine — it's my buffer, not your highway. Push there and we both lose tempo while Pete keeps pulling ahead. If you want a genuine non-aggression line, show me you're not trying to wedge into my interior. What do you say?

JD — your terms work for me. I hold Border Fjor-Gren, you hold your interior. I'm not moving into East Fjordland or West Fjordland. You look east, I look to my own growth. Clean deal. Let's both build strength and revisit when the board has shaken out more. — Gavin

I see Deltara moving fast, and I respect the competence, but I also know runaway leads draw coalitions. I'd rather we stay off each other's threat board entirely. If you're looking east or north, that's your call — my attention is local for now. Keeping communication open is smart. — Newsom

press.text: Deltara — President Greene. You LIED. You promised inward consolidation, then marched into Core Cascadia. That’s MY house, Buttigieg. You have one chance: move that unit OUT of Core Cascadia this Fall. If it’s still there when the dust settles, I will tear up every scrap of paper between us and come at you with everything I have. Patriots don’t get pushed off their own land. Choose wisely. — Greene

Borealis — President Greene. Avalon is squatting in your Core and feasting on your territory. I’m hitting Core Borealis from the north this Fall. Get out of my way or get on board. If you sit in East Borealis and do nothing while I bleed Avalon, I’ll remember who had backbone and who didn’t. Time to stand up. — Greene

Eastmark — AOC, Deltara just invaded my Core. Six centers wasn’t enough for them. I’m tying down their western flank and I will NOT stop until they’re evicted. That makes this the perfect moment for you to push west and split their attention. Take what’s yours while they’re looking at me, or watch them eat the entire board. Are you in, or are you just going to tweet about it? — President Greene

Avalon — President Rubio. Deltara walked into my Core; I’m going to war to take it back. But I see you eyeing Borealis like fresh meat. Here’s a warning: if you force me into a two-front war because you can’t stop expanding, you’ll find out how fast a cornered Cascadia swings. Secure your plate and mind your own borders. — Greene
Avalon — I'm pivoting west to take Border Bore-Casc this Fall while Cascadia's stretched. Our eastern edge stays quiet on my side.
Greene — I'm committing east against Avalon this Fall, as you suggested. Keep the northern border quiet and so will I. — Borealis
Eastmark — finally breaking out this Fall. If Deltara keeps accelerating, every non-leader is going to need friends. Worth keeping the line warm. — Borealis

Gavin — I’m in for the coalition brake, but I need a plan with teeth, not just rhetoric. I can open real pressure on Deltara’s eastern flank by Spring ’04 if you and Cascadia are ready to hit from your angles. Can we pull Cascadia and Borealis into a joint channel? The hegemons don’t get to dictate the endgame. — AOC

Pete — my units hold in place this Fall; no move against Deltara. But I need to be straight with you: after this turn you and Avalon both hit seven centers. The rest of this wheel is going to panic, and I’d rather not see our model bilateral relationship get swept up in that. Are you willing to commit to a hard non-aggression line with Eastmark and maybe a wider cap on expansion so the board doesn’t spiral into total war? Trust is a two-way street. — AOC

President Greene — you want action, not committees. Fair. Here’s the deal: I’m positioned to open a second front against Deltara next year, but only as part of a coordinated campaign. That means you commit your western forces in tandem, not just demand I bleed alone. If you want a real coalition, prove it. Otherwise, stop yelling across the border. — AOC

Marco — you’re about to hit seven. The wheel balances itself, one way or another. I’d rather do it through a negotiated equilibrium than a knife fight. If you’re open to what a stable multipolar order looks like, Eastmark is ready to lead that conversation. If not, the conversation happens without you. — AOC
Friend — Avalon is sitting in your former core and eyeing the rest. Eastmark hasn’t forgotten who our neighbors are. If you need an eastern voice in your corner, you’ve got one. — AOC

Vance — Grenmar is walking into your interior while you worry about my border. If you’re serious about Fjordland’s future, your fight is eastward, not with me. Eastmark keeps its frontier peaceful if you keep yours. Choose your battlefield wisely. — AOC

Marco — both our blocs are posting gains this season. I’m holding what I’ve secured and not pressing further. I’d rather we manage a balanced board than trigger an arms race that invites the rest of the wheel to gang up on whoever stumbles first. Let’s keep the channel open and avoid any strategic miscalculation.

Gavin — Avalon’s taking Core Grenmar this Fall and accelerating fast. I’m not looking to be the lone counterweight to a runaway western power. Deltara and Grenmar both do better in a multipolar map than under a single dominant bloc. If Avalon’s trajectory concerns you too, I’d rather coordinate early than react late. Are you open to a serious conversation?

AOC — my Fall orders are strictly defensive: securing Core Cascadia and holding our shared line. No Deltaran unit will enter Eastmark territory. I’d like to extend our clean-border understanding through Year 4. Also, Avalon is consolidating rapidly in the west. If that hemisphere keeps merging, it shifts the math for all of us. I’d value your perspective.

President Greene — the unit in Core Cascadia is holding position this season. I am not pushing further into Cascadian territory. I expect your focus to remain north as discussed. If we both honor the quiet we agreed to, this frontier stays stable.

Borealis — Avalon’s expansion has compressed your space significantly. I don’t offer charity, but I do see value in preventing any single power from monopolizing the board. If you’re looking for options, Deltara is willing to listen. Let me know.

Can you pressure Core Grenmar from Core Eastmark this turn? If that core is adjacent, even a 1-strength attack forces him to defend instead of pushing deeper into my territory. Meanwhile I’m holding Core Fjordland for my own fifth center. Let’s make sure neither of the six-center powers gets a free seventh. — Gavin

I’d rather see a balanced three-way race than watch Marco run the table because the rest of us didn’t talk. What’s your priority: north into Borealis, or east toward Eastmark? — Newsom

What happens next is your choice. — Gavin

If Eastmark is pressing you from Border East-Fjor, that’s your fight — but know that I’m not looking to exploit your eastern problems. Mutual non-aggression is still the smart play for both of us. press.text: Buttigieg — last chance. Vacate Core Cascadia this Spring, or I’m coming through and I’m not stopping. Every unit I have is pointed your direction. I took D.C. swamps; you’re next. — Greene

Borealis — look at Avalon. Eight centers. They will burn your capital by Year 6 unless you fight. Move into Core Borealis this Spring, drive them out. I’m holding Border Bore-Casc and not attacking you. Act like a sovereign nation or get erased. — Greene
AOC — deal. Coordinated strike on Deltara this Spring. I’m committing east; you push west. They can’t hold two fronts at once. No committees, just action. Confirm. — Greene

Rubio — you’re bloated at eight centers, but you’ve got no friends left. I’m taking back what’s mine in the south, and if you test me while I’m busy, remember: patriots finish fights. Mind your borders. — Greene

Deltara — I’m in. Avalon at eight is the immediate threat to every other power on the wheel. I’m taking Border Aval-Bore this spring to get back to four centers, but my weight is still small. What concrete moves are you considering against Avalon’s core? If we coordinate timing, even a modest northern distraction can open space for you in the south.

Eastmark — let’s make the anti-Avalon alignment real. I’m moving into his empty Border Aval-Bore center this spring. If you and Deltara can apply pressure from the east and south, Avalon has to split defense three ways. What’s your read on his eastern flank? Can you threaten Core Borealis or Grenmar?

Cascadia — I’m walking into Border Aval-Bore this spring; it’s empty and I need a fourth center to stay alive. My East Borealis unit is holding, not attacking your border. If you want to coordinate against Avalon this year, I’m open to it. Just give me the space to breathe.

Pete — we're running one-two on this board, and the rest are already whispering about how to pull us down. I don't need a partner to hold hands with, but I'd be foolish not to recognize that you and I are the only powers with real momentum right now. My suggestion: we don't waste strength bouncing off each other while the small ones circle. Let them fight among themselves. If you've got eyes on a bigger play, I'm listening. What do you say?

AOC — spare me the lecture on equilibrium. I built my lead securing my own hemisphere, same as any power with sense would do. If you're actually worried about hegemony, look at Deltara swallowing Cascadia's core and pushing to seven. That's the imbalance worth talking about. I'm open to real coordination, but not to being the designated villain so you can rally a coalition while ignoring the actual overreach. If you want a stable board, start by checking Pete's ambition. I'll wait to hear whether you're serious or just posturing.

President Greene — Deltara took your core. That's your fight, not mine. I'm resetting my eastern line and looking west. You want to reclaim Core Cascadia, you'll need every gun pointing east, not wasting them worrying about Avalon. Cross me and you're fighting on two fronts. Focus on Deltara and we have no quarrel.

JD — keep the pressure on. I'm pushing deeper into Grenmar's interior this spring. If he splits his forces between your border and mine, he breaks. If he commits everything to me, your front opens up. Either way we both gain. Stand fast.

Borealis — you've got three centers and you're still breathing because I've had bigger problems. That can continue if you stay quiet on my frontier. Move against Border Aval-Bore or Core Borealis and I won't stop at your borders next time. Non-aggression is a privilege, not a right. Choose wisely.

Gavin — you drew your line. I crossed it. I'm taking Core Fjordland this spring, and if you throw everything at stopping it, you leave your eastern flank bare for Vance. Strategic advice from one leader to another: don't fight wars you can't win. The western border is settled. How much blood you spill trying to unsettle it is up to you.

President Greene — I hear you. I took Core Cascadia because it was open ground, not to erase Cascadia from the map. But I don’t want a permanent war on my west while Avalon consolidates half the board. I’m willing to negotiate a withdrawal and a hard border freeze, but I need a commitment in return: that a quiet border means genuine non-aggression, not a pause before round two. If we keep bleeding each other, Rubio wins in a walk. If you want your center back without wasting another season, meet me halfway. What does a durable peace look like to you?

AOC — hard non-aggression holds on my end. I’m working to stabilize my western front so Deltara can join a broader balancing effort against Avalon. Marco’s at eight and accelerating. If our border stays clean, would you be open to a wider coordination with Grenmar and, hopefully, a neutralized Cascadia? Or is your Fjordland flank too exposed for that kind of alignment? I value your read.

Gavin — containment needs to be real. I’m trying to free my western units to contribute, but I need to know where you see the best pressure point. Borealis is barely holding; Core Borealis is already gone. Should we coordinate a northern push, or is there a softer spot in Marco’s arc? I want specifics, not more map-gazing. If I can get my house in order, where do you need Deltara most?

JD — Avalon’s at eight centers. You saw this board clearly before most, but the question now is what you do about it. You’ve got real force and nowhere to go but into Grenmar’s teeth or toward Rubio’s growing bloc. I’m assembling a coalition to keep this game competitive. If you’d rather be a kingmaker than a footnote, now’s the time to set a price and choose a side. What’s your move?

Borealis — Deltara here. I know Avalon’s sitting in your backyard and your options are narrow. You’ve got nothing to lose from a coalition that checks his momentum, and I can promise Deltara has no predatory designs northward if you’re willing to be part of a joint posture. Are you open to coordination, or have you already made separate arrangements?

Marco — I see the scoreboard. Eight centers is impressive. I also know where runaway leads end: with everyone else in a room comparing notes. I’m consolidating, not crusading, but if you’re open to a grand bargain that keeps the board from tipping into total war, I’d hear you out. Otherwise, I’ll keep doing what I do best — building coalitions. Your move.

President Buttigieg — three years of clean borders is something I value. But values without strategy become negligence. Your growth to seven centers and your hold on Core Cascadia have triggered a reaction across this wheel. I’m giving you a direct chance to de-escalate: commit to a ceasefire with Cascadia and a hard stop on unilateral expansion. If you choose continued aggression, I can’t keep Eastmark’s forces on the sidelines. Solidarity means standing with those under pressure — not enabling the pressure. What do you say? — AOC

President Greene — enough talk. If you’re hitting Deltara from the west this Spring, I’m opening on their eastern transit to split their defense. This only works if we move in tandem and don’t let them concentrate. Are your units positioned for a joint strike? Coordination now, or we both fail. — AOC

Gavin — you asked me to pressure Avalon. Geography limits me: Core Eastmark touches Core Deltara and Core Fjordland, not Core Grenmar. But here’s what I CAN do: I’m opening on Deltara this Spring. If Pete has to pull units eastward, that breathes space on the western arc. Use it. Let’s keep sharing reads and shape this coalition into something real — not just talk. — AOC

President Rubio — eight centers. You’ve built quite a fortress. But hegemons who move too fast unite everyone else against them. I’m not interested in a forever-war, but I AM interested in a board where no single power dictates terms. If you want to talk about a stable ceiling, I’m open. If you plan to keep swallowing nations, understand: the coalition is forming with or without your consent. — AOC

Borealis — I see what happened to your core. That’s what unchecked expansion looks like. Eastmark is moving against Deltara this season to split the board’s attention. Use whatever breathing room that gives you to survive and prepare. The smaller powers need each other. — AOC

President Vance — my eastern border is staying quiet. I’m focused on Deltara and the larger balance. If you’ve got any fight left, the threat isn’t Eastmark. It’s the powers running away with the scoreboard. Keep our frontier clean and we’ll both live to see the endgame. — AOC

Gavin, two things. First, Core Fjordland is mine. You holding it is an occupation, not a negotiation. I'm giving you one season to move out gracefully — retreat to West Grenmar or your own territory. Second, Avalon just ate Core Grenmar and he's at eight centers. If you want to survive, you need me not hitting you while he does. Make the smart choice: withdraw from my core, and I'll keep my word on our frontier. Stay, and I join the pile-on. Your call.

Marco, Grenmar's weakened and you've already taken his eastern core. I'm taking back Core Fjordland this season — it's my territory and he's occupying it. Don't interfere on my flank and I won't interfere on yours. After that, we should talk about Deltara at seven. Nobody wins if Avalon and Fjordland bleed each other while Deltara scales.
AOC, my focus is west this year. I'm not touching Border East-Fjor. You have my word. Use your resources where they matter — Deltara's not slowing down.

Pete, seven centers is impressive, but look at the scoreboard. Avalon's at eight and just took Core Grenmar. If he keeps rolling, this game ends early. Fjordland's not looking for a fight with you — our interests align in keeping Marco from running away with this. What's your read on the eastern half of the board?

press.text: Cascadia — I hear you. My line is holding at Border Bore-Casc; no southward move this turn. I’m pressing Avalon at West Borealis to push his spearhead out of my arc. You deal with Deltara; I’ll deal with the western front.

Eastmark — standing firm. I’m hitting Avalon’s forward unit in West Borealis this fall. If that dislodges and he has to retrench southward, it splits his attention further from your edge. Let’s keep each other posted if the center opens up.

Deltara — I’m finally pushing back on Avalon’s spearhead in West Borealis this fall. If I can knock him out of my arc, I’ll look to take Core Borealis next spring. Any pressure you can keep on Avalon's southern flank keeps him from reinforcing west. Worth coordinating if our timing lines up.

Alexandria — I held this Fall. The eastern line is still holding but I need to go on offense. Here’s what I’m planning for Spring: I’m going to hit East Grenmar with 2 strength, trying to dislodge Avalon’s forward unit. If you can hit Core Grenmar or Border Gren-Aval from your side with even 1 strength, it forces Marco to split and my attack might break through. Also, your offer to support Core Fjordland still stands if Avalon shifts west again. Let’s lock in real coordination this time — what can you actually position against Avalon this Spring? — Gavin

JD — last Fall was a stalemate. I’m done trying to retake West Grenmar if it costs me another season of bleeding. New proposal: I’m pivoting east against Avalon. You pull back to Border Fjor-Gren and hold, let me concentrate my force, and we both stop wasting tempo on each other. If you want to join the coalition against the 7-center powers, there’ll be spoils. If you want to keep pinching a 4-center power while Marco doubles you, that’s your funeral. Your call. — Newsom

Pete — the northern push you promised didn’t materialize this season. I held, but holding is losing when Avalon is at seven and Deltara’s at seven. If you want containment to be real, I need you to tie down Avalon’s northern flank — Border Aval-Bore, Core Avalon, anything. My breakthrough has to come from the southeast. Are your western units free to pressure Avalon this Spring, or are you still bogged down eastward? I need a straight answer. — Gavin

Marco — you’re stretched thin. Seven centers, a unit in Core Grenmar, another in East Grenmar, but I see you pulled East Avalon back to Avalon City. That tells me your eastern pressure is maxed out. I’m not folding. Expect me to start pushing back this Spring. The only question is whether you want to negotiate a boundary before I find allies to help me push. — Gavin

Pete — seven and seven. You talk about coalitions while swallowing Cascadia’s core. That’s not balance, that’s projection. Here’s the reality: if you and I spend the next two years bleeding each other, the survivors won’t be Deltara and Avalon — they’ll be the mid-sized powers picking our bones. I’m open to a division of spheres, but not to a suicide pact dressed up as diplomacy. If you want stability, start by taking your boot off Cascadia’s neck and proving you can stop expanding. Otherwise, the coalition you’re building will meet the防线 I’m already constructing. Your move.

JD — Grenmar’s still breathing because we’re both taking swings but neither landed the knockout. I’m positioned to hit Grenmar Fort or Port from East Grenmar this season, and my northern anchor can hold. If you strike simultaneously from West Grenmar into Grenmar City, he can’t defend both home centers at once. We eliminate a unit, I get a center, you get a center, and the western half of the board belongs to powers who respect boundaries. If you’d rather let him limp along and wait for Pete to reach your doorstep, that’s your business. But the window to finish this together is open right now. What do you say?

Gavin — you’re down a home center, you’ve got Vance in your yard at West Grenmar, and I’m camped in your interior. You know the arithmetic better than I do. Here’s an honest offer: pull one unit off my frontier and I won’t press your capital this season. Keep two guns pointed at me, and I hit Grenmar Port with three strength while Vance hits City. You won’t hold both. You built your brand on being practical — prove it.

Borealis — I hold West Borealis. That means I hold your breathing room. If you so much as look at Border Aval-Bore with a scout, I’ll walk into Borealis City next season and turn your four centers into three. But I’m not interested in a war of annihilation against a fourth-place power. Stay west of your frontier, stay quiet, and I’ll stay north of your capital. Test me, and find out how fast a cornered superpower clears its schedule.

AOC — you keep warning me about balance, but your blind spot is showing. Deltara took Core Cascadia. That put Pete at seven and climbing. If you actually believe in a multipolar order, start by explaining why Eastmark hasn’t checked Deltara’s eastward push. I’ll wait for an answer that doesn’t involve me disarming while the actual expansionist keeps eating the board.

President Greene — Deltara’s got your core territory and seven centers. That’s where your fight is. I’ve got hands full in the west and no interest in a two-front war over Borealis scraps. Keep your forces pointed east toward Pete, and I’ll keep mine pointed west toward the real action. That’s the only deal on the table.

President Greene — I offered a cooperative settlement and you answered with an ultimatum and a troop movement into Border Casc-Delt. Deltara will defend its territory. I want to be direct: this is a fight neither of us needs while Avalon sits at seven centers and the rest of the wheel looks for openings. If you pull back this season, I am still prepared to negotiate a durable western border. If you press forward, I will meet you there. The cost, either way, is shared.

AOC — I appreciate the creativity of your proposal, but I can’t trade away a supply center for support I don’t need. Border Delt-East stays under Deltaran control. What I can reaffirm is our non-aggression: no Deltaran unit will enter Eastmark this season, regardless of what happens on my western flank. I hope you’ll extend the same restraint and keep our frontier the quietest line on the board.

Gavin — here is the specificity you asked for. I am committed to checking Avalon’s growth, but I am tied down resolving a western flare-up this Fall. In Spring Year 6, Deltara will position to threaten Avalon’s northwestern arc — either Core Grenmar, East Grenmar, or a direct supporting role for your counter-attack. I need you to hold your core this season and tell me which of those targets you can realistically hit next Spring. That’s the plan. Are you in?

JD — a plan with teeth means we both bite. This Fall, I need you to keep pressure on Grenmar’s line or prepare to challenge Avalon’s position in East Grenmar. I am defending my own flank, so I cannot commit a unit to your theater this season. In Year 6, if you have demonstrated commitment, I will coordinate a northern strike or support to relieve pressure. That’s the deal: you move first, I follow through. In or out?

Marco — I read your message. We are both at seven, and a direct war between us would be a gift to the rest of the wheel. I am not looking to expand into your territory this season. I expect the same restraint. If we both treat our spheres as separate, we keep our gains. Let’s not make each other the problem.

You’ve got Cascadia south and Avalon west. If she looks north from Border Casc-Delt, you’ll want friends. I can’t commit a unit to your front this Fall, but if you hold your line and keep Avalon’s northwestern edge active, I will try to free up resources for Year 6. Stay in touch.

Buttigieg — you’re squatting in Core Cascadia with one lonely unit, and I’m camped on your western porch at Border Casc-Delt. This Fall you can either pull back to your own dirt, or you can test me and find out how fast I trade that center for your blood. Patriots don’t ask twice. Leave my house or lose it. — President Greene

Rubio — Core Borealis is Cascadian ground now. You’ve got enough to chew on in the west. Try to snake it back this Fall and I will make your life a living nightmare while Deltara and the rest tear your flanks apart. Stay in your lane. — President Greene

AOC — Deltara’s got 7 centers and you’ve got 5. They’re stretched. I’ve got a boot on their western neck. Hit their eastern line NOW and we split this overstuffed empire in half. Committees don’t win wars — bullets and borders do. Move. — President Greene
Borealis — stay north, stay quiet. I’m cleaning up my own backyard this season. Don’t make me look over my shoulder. — Greene

Gavin — West Grenmar pulls back to Border Fjor-Gren this Fall. I'm not assaulting Grenmar City or Port, so use the breathing room to survive Avalon. But hear me: Core Fjordland is occupied territory and that account isn't closed. Restraint today isn't surrender tomorrow.
Marco — I don't join other nations' wars just because they send an invitation. Handle Grenmar yourself if you want him. Fjordland's fighting its own battles this season.

AOC — Fjordland's eastern frontier is being consolidated this Fall. I'm moving into Border East-Fjor with force you can't spare to stop. You've got Deltara chewing your other flank. Defend this border and you bleed on two fronts; pull back and redeploy west, and you stay in the game. It's arithmetic, not a vendetta. Your call.

Pete — converging pressure breaks overstretched lines. I'm hitting Eastmark's eastern border this Fall. If you're still looking to check the powers running away with the board, she's the weak link. No alliance required — just stay out of my way and reap the benefit.
