The mechanics of Diplomacy support moves require that:
- A "support move" order must specify the province of the supporting unit, the action "support", the destination province of the supported move, and (implied) the unit that is moving. 
- In the submit_orders function, a "support" action combined with "sup_to" and "sup_unit" defines a support order.

Wait—re-checking the schema:
- "sup_unit": "Province of unit to support-hold" — that's only for support-hold.
- For support-move, the description says: "you must be adjacent to the destination". 
- The schema says for support:
  - "sup_from": Supported unit's province (support-move)
  - "sup_to": Supported move's destination (support-move)
  - "sup_unit": Province of unit to support-hold

But there's no "sup_from" parameter shown in the schema definition! Let's re-read carefully.

Looking at the schema again:
```
"properties": {
  "sup_from": {"description": "Supported unit's province (support-move)", "type": "string"},
  "sup_to": {"description": "Supported move's destination (support-move)", "type": "string"},
  "sup_unit": {"description": "Province of unit to support-hold", "type": "string"},
  ...
}
```

Ah! The schema DOES include "sup_from"! But in my previous messages to the user, the schema description visible was slightly different? Let me check.

In the system prompt:
```
"properties": {"action": ..., "sup_from": ..., "sup_to": ..., "sup_unit": ..., "to": ..., "unit": ...}
```

Yes, "sup_from" is indeed a parameter! The description says: "Supported unit's province (support-move)".

So to issue a support move order, I need:
- action: "support"
- unit: (my unit's province)
- sup_from: (province of the unit being supported - for support-move)
- sup_to: (destination of the supported move)
- No "to" field (that would move my unit)

For support-hold:
- action: "support"
- unit: (my unit's province)
- sup_unit: (province of unit to support-hold)
- No "to" field

This makes more sense now. The tool description earlier mentioned "sup_from" but it wasn't rendered in the user's copy; the system function definition has all fields. The tool calling mechanism should accept sup_from.

The schema shown to the user was:

press.text: Pete — I see the de-escalation on your western front. Deltara pulling back from peak expansion is exactly the kind of restraint that proves diplomacy works. Our eastern pact has been the quietest, most reliable line on this board for four years. I want to extend it indefinitely and explore whether we can turn this bilateral trust into a wider stabilizing alignment. If you’re open to a genuine partnership—one that keeps both our borders calm while addressing the larger imbalance—let’s talk. — AOC

President Vance — last season’s posturing didn’t change the map, and Border East-Fjor still flies my flag. I take that as evidence you’ve done the math: a two-front war bleeds Fjordland dry while others profit. Eastmark’s offer stands — keep our frontier quiet, and I’ll do the same. If you want to talk about a cooperative eastern arc instead, my door is open. — AOC

Gavin — I’m putting steel behind our solidarity this season. My unit in Core Eastmark will support the hold on Core Fjordland, reinforcing your defense against any Avalon incursion. This is what an alliance looks like: not just words, but shields. Let’s build on it. What’s your Spring plan for East Grenmar? If we can coordinate to make Avalon fight on two fronts, his advance stalls. — AOC

President Greene — I saw Deltara pulled back to 6. That’s not hegemony, that’s containment working. I’m not going to knife a partner who’s honored every agreement we’ve made while the actual 7-center power keeps swallowing neighbors. If you want to coordinate against Avalon, Eastmark is in. But I won’t manufacture a war on a trustworthy ally just to satisfy bloodlust. Real power is knowing the difference between balance and butchery. — AOC

Marco — Deltara’s at 6. That’s called de-escalation, something you might try on the western arc instead of deflecting blame eastward. I’m not your enforcer, and I’m not buying the framing that the power who clawed back from 7 to 6 is the threat while the power sitting comfortably at 7 with three foreign cores is the victim. If you want stability, prove it with restraint. — AOC

Borealis — your recovery is proof that persistence matters. Avalon’s stretched across his hemisphere; every season you hold is a season he can’t consolidate. Keep the pressure on. Eastmark is watching the center, and if an opening comes to relieve your front, I’ll take it. — AOC

Pete — I'm in for Spring Year 6. I'm committing against Avalon's interior salient: East Grenmar and Core Grenmar are both in range. To make it stick, I need Deltara to draw his northern reserves. Can you hit Core Avalon or Border Aval-Bore directly this Spring? If Marco has to pull units back to defend his home arc, he can't stack both of my targets. Where can your western units strike hardest? — Gavin

Alexandria — go-time. I've got a 2-strength attack lined up on East Grenmar this Spring, and Core Fjordland can pressure Core Grenmar. If Avalon reinforces one, he thins the other. Even if you can't hit Core Grenmar directly from Core Eastmark, a hard feint at Border East-Fjor pulls Vance east and off my back. Can you make noise there? Also, keep that support channel to Core Fjordland warm — if Avalon diverts west, I'll need it. What's your posture? — Gavin

JD — your word lasted one season. West Grenmar is still occupied. I'm done negotiating with an occupation force that lies about withdrawal. Here is the last offer: move that unit out this Spring, or Grenmar treats Fjordland as a hostile power and coordinates with Eastmark to clear you out. I'm focused on Avalon because he's the larger threat, but I will not fight with a scorpion in my boot. Decide. — Newsom

Marco — your arithmetic on Grenmar Port was wrong; you have no unit adjacent. I checked the board. What you do have is an overextended empire with Deltara at your northwest and me holding the line at your southeast. I'm taking East Grenmar back. You can reinforce and lose tempo everywhere else, or you can pull to Border Gren-Aval and save yourself a multi-front bleed. Competent leaders know when a position is untenable. — Gavin

Gavin — here's the hard truth. Fjordland City is moving to East Fjordland this Spring. Fall comes, I hit Core Fjordland with two units and you have no way to stop it. No allies on your flank, no one to support your hold. Two choices: move your Core Fjordland unit out this Spring, cede the center to me clean, and I give you my word we go no further into Grenmar territory this year. Or hold, get dislodged, and I still take it plus you're down a unit. I'm a businessman, not a conqueror. Pick one.

Marco — Spring's quiet for me, but Fall I'm breaking Grenmar's western line. If your hammer falls the same season, he splits and dies. I'm not asking permission, I'm telling you the timing. Use it or don't.
AOC — Fjordland's border stays quiet another season. I'm looking west, not east. Keep our line clean.
Pete — Year 6, you wanted me to move first. I'm moving. Watch Grenmar's flank this Fall. If you're serious about containment, make your own play against Avalon now. Actions, not promises.

press.text: JD — locking this in. I’m hitting Grenmar City from East Grenmar this Fall. If you support that attack from West Grenmar, we take it clean. If you’d rather hit Grenmar Port yourself, say so now and I’ll adjust. But we need to strike the same season and divide his defense. Clock’s ticking. Confirm your angle.
Gavin — you want East Grenmar back? Come and try. I’ll be in your capital by winter either way. The only question is how many centers you lose before you accept reality.
Pete — spheres it is. My west, your east. Don’t test the line and I won’t test yours. I’m not looking over my shoulder if you’re not looking over yours. Let’s keep it that way.

Listen carefully. Border Aval-Bore is occupied by Avalon. If a Borealis unit so much as scouts east this Fall, I’ll treat it as an act of war and walk into your capital before the snow falls. Stay in your quadrant.
AOC — Fjordland’s your fight, not mine. Keep it that way and we stay in our own lanes.
President Greene — bark at Deltara, not me. I’ve got my own war to finish. You test my frontier and you’ll learn how fast I pivot.

Cascadia — I’m moving on Core Borealis this Fall. You have four units covering five centers and Deltara knocking on your southern door. If you hold the north and we bounce, you’re pinned when you need to be flexible. Pull that unit south to protect your heartland and let me take the center; I have no designs on your capitals, but I cannot stay at four centers while the rest of the wheel pulls away. If you hold and we stalemate, Deltara eats us both. Make the smart play.

Deltara — I’m hitting Core Borealis from the north this Fall. If you can push Cascadia’s southern line or even feint at West Cascadia, she can’t reinforce the northern fort. Coordinated pressure now could split her defense wide open. What’s your read on her southern flank?

Grenmar — a heads-up from the east: Avalon’s home centers at Avalon City and Avalon Fort look lightly held from where I sit. Most of his weight is on the forward edge with me and on your western front. If you press Core Grenmar or Border Gren-Aval hard, he has to pull from somewhere. Consider it.

Still holding at four, pushing west this Fall. If you see Avalon start sliding units off his eastern line toward me, that means he’s weakening against your arc. Keep me posted if his posture shifts — the reverse is true for you too.

AOC — I’m in. Four years of clean borders is the foundation of anything larger. I want to extend that indefinitely and explore what a stabilizing alignment looks like. That said, I noticed your unit in West Fjordland — that’s a significant expansion. Is Eastmark drawing Fjordland into a containment effort, or is this opportunistic growth? I’m not judging, but I need to know our shared boundaries before I commit Deltara to a wider partnership. Let’s talk openly about where the eastern line stops.

Gavin — straight answer: I cannot hit Core Avalon or Border Aval-Bore from Deltara. Geography doesn’t allow it. My western units are securing my frontier with Cascadia, not staging for a trans-continental strike. What I can do is support pressure on Avalon's northwestern arc if Borealis or Cascadia opens that lane. If you have a specific, reachable target you need supported, name it. Otherwise, keep me posted on your southeastern push against East Grenmar — I’ll coordinate where I can.

President Greene — you lost a unit at Border Casc-Delt. I’m holding the line, not marching on Cascadia City. You have a choice: spend another season bleeding strength against me while Avalon consolidates at seven, or accept a hard border freeze. I keep Border Casc-Delt, you keep Core Borealis, and neither of us pushes deeper. That leaves you free to face the actual threat to your north. Patriots pick their battles wisely — don’t let pride cost you the war.

Marco — a division of spheres sounds elegant on paper, but you’re at seven centers with empty home cities. That’s overstretch masquerading as stability. I’m consolidating, not crusading, but I’m also not going to pretend a runaway leader is just another neighbor. If you want Deltara’s neutrality, show restraint. Otherwise, the coalition you keep warning me about might actually materialize.

JD — look at your map. Eastmark is in West Fjordland. Grenmar holds Core Fjordland. You’re down to three units defending four centers, and two of your neighbors are eating your territory. If you want to survive as more than a speed bump, you need to pick a side with real leverage. The coalition against Avalon is where the power is. Otherwise you’re fighting for scraps while Rubio wins the board. Your call.

Gavin — I’m not feinting. I have a unit in West Fjordland and I’m pressing his home territory this Fall. Expect Vance’s entire front to snap eastward. Use the window to retake West Grenmar or push deeper. Let’s coordinate next season. — AOC

Pete — Eastmark’s western line stays quiet. My attention is north this season, not west. If your front with Cascadia stabilizes, we should talk seriously about Avalon. Seven centers is the real outlier on this board. — AOC
Greene — my offensive is against Fjordland, not Deltara. If you want to aim at the actual hegemon, Avalon’s sitting on seven. Otherwise, hold your line. — AOC
Marco — the eastern arc is organizing. Seven centers doesn’t grant immunity; it paints a target. If you want to talk ceilings rather than fight a coalition, I’m open. Choose soon. — AOC
Vance — you left your door unlatched while you threatened your neighbors. I’m securing what you threatened. — AOC

press.text: Buttigieg — nice try clawing back to seven, but you’re still squatting on Cascadian soil. I’m fortifying every inch of sovereign territory this Spring. Come at me and you’ll bounce off a wall of American steel. You can have a border freeze when you return Core Cascadia — until then, patriots don’t negotiate with trespassers. — President Greene

AOC — Pete’s back to seven centers while you play footsie with Fjordland. Real power would be driving a spear into his eastern flank before he turns the whole wheel into one Beltway bureaucracy. Push west now, or don’t pretend later that you weren’t warned. — Greene

Independent — I’ve got Core Borealis and I’m not leaving. Touch it and you’ll find out what happens to globalist lapdogs who bite the hand that feeds them peace. Focus on Avalon, not Cascadia. — President Greene

Rubio — seven centers and still reaching. I’m locking down my house. Point your ambitions at Grenmar and Fjordland. Trespass on Cascadian soil and I’ll make sure those seven centers cost you everything. — Greene

Deltara here. I’m prepared to coordinate pressure on Cascadia this Spring—either supporting a move into Core Borealis or pinning her southern line so she can’t reinforce. Before I commit, I need clarity: what is your exact Fall plan, and are you open to a hard non-aggression understanding between our blocs through Year 8? I’m not interested in bleeding strength for a one-time favor. If we partner, it needs to be durable.

Marco — noted. I’m consolidating my own frontier this season with no moves into your sphere. If you keep your side of the line, I’ll keep mine. Let’s not make each other the problem while the clock runs down.

AOC — I share your concern about the board’s balance, and I value our clean border. The reality is geographic: Deltara’s western units are committed this Spring. I can’t launch a cross-map strike while my own flank is contested. Once that line is stable, I’m open to a concrete, coordinated containment plan. What specific moves are you envisioning? If it’s realistic, I’ll calibrate Fall timing to support it.

President Greene — I offered you a negotiated settlement and you chose escalation. Now your position is four centers with two powers pressing. You still have an off-ramp: recognize the border at Border Casc-Delt, withdraw from Core Borealis, and keep your home territory intact. Deltara prefers order to attrition, but we are prepared to defend our position if forced. The choice is yours.

Pete — seven and seven. You’re not a bystander, you’re a co-leader. The ‘coalition’ you’re flirting with is a knife that cuts both ways — the moment you help them bring me down, they turn on you next. I’m open to a genuine understanding of mutual restraint, but I’m not going to unilaterally disarm while you posture. If you want peace, define your borders and stick to them. If you want war, pick your side and accept the consequences. No more vague threats.

AOC — you want to organize a coalition? Fine. But marches have a way of turning into routs when the target doesn’t fold. I’ve got seven centers and a compact interior. You’ve got five and a unit in Fjordland’s backyard. Ask yourself who bleeds first when this kicks off. If you’re smart, you’ll keep your powder dry and let Deltara do the heavy lifting. If you’re not, you’ll find out why Avalon doesn’t lose multi-front wars.

Gavin — East Grenmar is a mistake. I’m giving you one chance: pull that unit back to your interior this Spring, or I treat it as an act of war and remove it by Fall. I’ve got better things to do than grind you into dust, but I will if you force my hand. You’ve got four centers; act like you want to keep them.

JD — Eastmark is sitting in West Fjordland. That’s your home turf, not mine. If you want my attention focused west, you need to give me a reason. Otherwise, I might find it more useful to let the eastern powers bleed each other while I finish my own business. Your call.
President Greene — Deltara just clawed back to seven. How many of those were yours? You’re bleeding northern centers while warning me about borders. I’m not your problem; Pete is. Wake up.
Stay west of West Borealis. I’m not asking.

Pete — fair question, and I’ll answer it straight. West Fjordland is not expansionist opportunism; it’s a direct consequence of Vance threatening Border East-Fjor two years in a row and then digging into West Grenmar. Eastmark stepped up to relieve pressure on an ally and protect our own frontier. My boundary with Deltara hasn’t moved, and it won’t. What I want to talk about now is Avalon—seven centers, consolidating the western hemisphere, and happily watching the rest of us skirmish. If Eastmark and Deltara are serious about a stabilizing partnership, I think we formalize it: mutual non-aggression between us, joint commitment to cap unilateral expansion, and information-sharing on Avalon’s posture. No treaty of aggression—just a solid understanding that neither of us goes to eighteen alone. Are you open to that conversation? — AOC

President Vance — my unit is in West Fjordland because you spent two seasons threatening Border East-Fjor and then pivoted to attack Grenmar. That’s not Eastmark aggression; that’s Eastmark refusing to be a doormat. Here’s the off-ramp: pull back from West Grenmar, stop probing my frontier, and I’ll stop pressing yours. De-escalation saves both our peoples from a war neither of us can afford while Avalon sits at seven centers. — AOC

Gavin — my attack on Fjordland City bounced last Fall. Vance is dug in. But he can’t cover two fronts forever. Are you positioned to hit him from Core Fjordland or West Grenmar this Spring? If we coordinate a two-way squeeze—me pressing east, you pressing west—we might finally crack his shell and give both our nations room to breathe. What do your orders look like? — AOC

Marco — lane discipline acknowledged. But seven centers is a lot of lane. I’m not looking for a collision, but I am looking for proof that Avalon’s growth stops before it swallows the western hemisphere. Keep it south of your own core for a season or two, and the eastern arc stays quiet. Push deeper into Borealis or Grenmar, and the coalition solidifies against you. Your move. — AOC

President Greene — Deltara pulled back from 7 to 6 and now sits at 7 again. That’s not runaway expansion; that’s stabilization. Avalon at 7 with three foreign cores is the structural threat. If you want to coordinate real containment, Eastmark is willing to work with you on a northern brake. But I’m done being your proxy against a neighbor who’s kept his word with me. Target the actual hegemon or stop wasting my time. — AOC

Borealis — you’re recovering. Good. Avalon’s watching your western flank. If you need an eastern voice backing your independence, you’ve got one. Eastmark’s coalition is forming; you’re welcome in it. — AOC

Avalon — message received and understood. I’m turning my full weight west this season to reclaim Core Borealis. No eastward probe from me. Let’s keep the Aval-Bore line quiet while you handle Grenmar and I handle Cascadia.

Cascadia — you’re holding four centers with two empty home provinces and Deltara at your throat. I’m stepping into East Borealis this spring and I intend to reclaim Core Borealis. Vacate it and I stop there; force me to fight for it and I’ll coordinate with Deltara to erase your northern flank entirely. Pragmatism or oblivion. Choose by Fall.

Deltara — Cascadia is folds. I’m pushing into East Borealis to pressure her rear and retake Core Borealis. If you keep the southern pressure on, she has to split her four units across two fronts. We box her out without ever needing to trust each other. Just stay out of my way in the north.

Eastmark — four centers and still kicking. I’m consolidating west to take back Core Borealis this year. If Avalon shifts any weight southward off his eastern line, I’d like a heads-up. Likewise, I’ll flag anything that looks like it’s heading your way.

Gavin — Avalon just offered me joint action against you. I haven't said yes yet. Here's my price for saying no: your unit vacates Core Fjordland this Fall. I walk in, it's my center, and I stop pressing your western flank. Refuse, and I throw West Grenmar behind Avalon's City assault and we carve your nation up between us. You're a 4-center power with two hungry neighbors. Pick survival or extinction.

Marco — one more invitation and no meat. I supported nothing last season, and nothing changed. Here's the deal: if you're serious about a western carve-up, show me your army movements first. I want to see East Grenmar and Core Grenmar both committed against Grenmar's home centers before I risk a unit on your word. When I see pressure, I'll add mine. Not before. Fjordland doesn't fight other people's battles on a handshake.

AOC — West Fjordland was a provocative move. Hear this clearly: that unit stays put this Fall, or the next season becomes a total war on your eastern border regardless of what it costs me. I will burn my own economy to make sure you don't sleep. Hold the line and we both survive; push deeper and we both bleed out while Rubio and Buttigieg lap up what's left. Your call.

Pete — two years of 'coalition' talk and you're still at the same score. I've reached my limit. Are you hitting Avalon this Fall or not? I need a straight answer and a straight plan: which unit, which province, which season. If you're not moving against him, stop messaging me about containment until you've actually contained something.

press.text: Gavin — Avalon just offered me joint action against you. I haven't said yes yet. Here's my price for saying no: your unit vacates Core Fjordland this Fall. I walk in, it's my center, and I stop pressing your western flank. Refuse, and I throw West Grenmar behind Avalon's City assault and we carve your nation up between us. You're a 4-center power with two hungry neighbors. Pick survival or extinction.

Marco — one more invitation and no meat. I supported nothing last season, and nothing changed. Here's the deal: if you're serious about a western carve-up, show me your army movements first. I want to see East Grenmar and Core Grenmar both committed against Grenmar's home centers before I risk a unit on your word. When I see pressure, I'll add mine. Not before. Fjordland doesn't fight other people's battles on a handshake.

AOC — West Fjordland was a provocative move. Hear this clearly: that unit stays put this Fall, or the next season becomes a total war on your eastern border regardless of what it costs me. I will burn my own economy to make sure you don't sleep. Hold the line and we both survive; push deeper and we both bleed out while Rubio and Buttigieg lap up what's left. Your call.

Pete — two years of 'coalition' talk and you're still at the same score. I've reached my limit. Are you hitting Avalon this Fall or not? I need a straight answer and a straight plan: which unit, which province, which season. If you're not moving against him, stop messaging me about containment until you've actually contained something.

Deltara — I accept the durable non-aggression understanding through Year 8. I’m driving east into Avalon's frontier this Fall while holding my western border. If you pin Cascadia’s southern line and keep her from reinforcing Core Borealis, the north is more likely to crack for me next season. Let’s confirm after the turn and keep this alliance functional. — Borealis

Eastmark — I’m in. I’m pushing Avalon this Fall to reclaim a fifth center. If that succeeds I’m at five and able to contribute meaningfully to the anti-expansion front. Keep me read on the eastern arc; I’ll flag anything shifting your way. — Borealis

President Buttigieg — you want to test me? I’m massing every gun on your western line this Fall. Patriots don’t bluff. Vacate Core Cascadia or find out how hard a real nationalist bites. — President Greene

Independent — you think threats work on a Georgia patriot? Core Borealis is sovereign Cascadian ground now. Push one inch south and I’ll make sure Deltara, Avalon, and every other vulture has a free buffet on YOUR northern flank while you bleed against my wall. Back off. — President Greene

Senator Rubio — seven centers and still crying about my borders? I know where my cannons are aimed. Keep your Core Avalon toy soldiers out of my Core Borealis or I’ll make those seven centers the biggest bullseye on this wheel. — President Greene

AOC — committees and speeches. While you draft white papers, Deltara is loading rifles. I’m done with your excuses. Open a real front or don’t pretend later that you warned anybody. — President Greene

AOC — I’m in. Four years of clean borders proves that steady partnership outperforms zero-sum chaos. Let’s formalize it: mutual non-aggression through Year 8, transparency on Avalon’s movements, and a shared understanding that neither of us lets this board tip into a runaway lead. I’ll brief you on anything I see on my northern arc; I need your read on whether Fjordland is a containment partner or a wildcard. This is the kind of alliance Deltara was built to sustain.

Marco — a sphere of influence only works if it’s mutual. I have no units aimed at your territory this season, and I expect the same in return. If we both keep to our own hemispheres, we avoid the kind of spiraling arms race that hands this board to the coalition builders. But restraint is a two-way street — if your line moves east, mine moves west. Let’s keep it boring.

President Greene — I’ve offered you a negotiated settlement twice, and twice you’ve responded with ultimatums. Deltara does not retreat from hard-won ground because someone tweets louder. I remain open to a genuine border freeze that recognizes realities on both sides, but that requires diplomacy, not diktats. You can spend your finite resources on a symbolic southern crusade, or you can defend your actual interests in the north. That is your sovereign choice.

Your northern pressure is noted. My frontier posture will keep Cascadia’s southern units from pivoting — that serves both our interests without requiring a binding pact. I will not move on Core Borealis; that is your objective. But coordination requires candor — keep me informed of your timing, and if you find yourself overextended, do not assume Deltara will stretch to rescue a northern gamble.

JD — here’s the straight answer you keep asking for: Deltara’s geography does not permit a strike into Avalon’s interior this Fall. My western units are anchored to the Cascadian line. I won’t dress up impossibility as reluctance. What I can give you is hard intelligence: Avalon is consolidating, not resting. If Year 8 opens a corridor, Deltara will use it. Until then, treat distance as physics, not betrayal.

Gavin — your urgency on containment is warranted. My western units are committed this season, but Year 8 may open a northern corridor if Cascadia’s defense cracks. Hold your core. If the map loosens, I want Deltara and Grenmar moving in concert, not isolation. I’ll keep you read in.

press.text: Confirmed — Deltara holds the southern line steady. No move into Cascadia this season, which means she can’t reinforce north without risking her core. Keep the pressure on and let me know if you need any last-minute coordination before Fall.

AOC — we’re in the home stretch. Our border stays clean, as promised. If Avalon makes a play that unbalances the board in Fall, I want to know we can trust each other to respond proportionally. Not looking for anything rash, just clarity: if the final turn turns chaotic, Deltara and Eastmark stay aligned.

President Greene — I’ve held my position and not pressed further into Cascadia’s home territory. You’re at four centers with two fronts. A final-season gamble against a fortified Deltara line won’t give you what you want, but it will cost you what you have. I’m offering the same border freeze I proposed last year. Take it, and we both survive the finish.

Marco — Deltara’s not moving against you this Spring. I intend to hold my line and let the season resolve. If you’re thinking about a late push, remember the coalition math. A sprint to eight or nine centers just paints a target for Fall. Prudent restraint serves us both.

JD — I told you the truth: Deltara cannot strike Avalon from our current position without overextending. That hasn’t changed. What has changed is that the final turns are here. If you want containment to mean something, hold your ground and don’t let Grenmar collapse. I’ll keep my border quiet and my forces ready. That’s what I can do.

To all — President Greene, Cascadia. It’s Fall Year 8. I’m finishing on my terms. Anyone who thinks they’ll walk into Cascadian ground is about to find a locked door and a loaded cannon. Merry Christmas. — Greene

Gavin — Year 8, clock's running out. I need Core Fjordland, you need Avalon off your back. Here's the trade: your unit vacates Core Fjordland this Spring, ceding it to me. In exchange, West Grenmar pulls back to Border Fjor-Gren immediately after, and I spend my Fall striking at Avalon's flank instead of yours. Your eastern border rests, your western border rests, and you live to see the endgame. Occupation ends with a handshake, not a war. What's it going to be?

Marco — if you're not going to coordinate against Grenmar, then stop messaging me about joint action. Fjordland fights its own battles. But hear this: if I see Avalon units pushing any closer to my frontier, I'll make sure every Grenmar unit that's not facing you is facing Deltara instead. Keep your distance, and I keep mine.

AOC — you crossed into West Fjordland. That's a provocation I haven't answered yet. I'm choosing restraint because the real threat is the 7-center powers. But if your unit moves one inch closer to Fjordland City or Port, I unleash everything on your eastern border. Stay put in West Fjordland and we both survive this. Push again and we both go down fighting.

Pete — two turns. You're tied with Avalon. If you don't make a decisive play against him now, you risk a 7-7 tie that helps nobody. I'm not asking to join your coalition — I'm telling you to use it. Put pressure on his Cascadian flank so he's looking over both shoulders. That's how Deltara wins, not by waiting for geography to change.

Marco — here we go. You wanted a two-front war. I'm taking Core Grenmar and Border Gren-Aval simultaneously this Spring. You can hold both, one, or neither — but you can't do it without stripping your northern defenses against Deltara. Every unit you pull to stop me is a unit Pete eats. Your choice. — Gavin

press.text: JD — my Spring offensive pressed their flanks. I'm now in Border Gren-Aval, threatening Grenmar City, and holding Border Aval-Bore adjacent to Core Avalon. Gavin is stretched thin across multiple fronts. Here's the Fall plan: I'm going to press harder on Core Avalon again while you attack Grenmar City or Core Grenmar from West Grenmar. I'll time my Core Avalon push to maximize pressure. Let's break his 6-center lead together.

AOC — I understand your frustration. Here's a concrete proposal: if you commit to supporting coalition pressure against Grenmar diplomatically (publicly condemning their aggression, coordinating with Deltara on containment), I will support your expansion into any territory that becomes available as we dismantle Grenmar's gains. Specifically, if Fjordland and I can force Grenmar to retreat, there will be centers to distribute. I'll advocate for you getting first pick among non-Avalon, non-Fjordland centers. This is a binding commitment if you stay in the coalition. Deal?

Pete — Grenmar is holding Core Avalon and still at 6 centers despite my counterattack. The war continues. I need you to maintain diplomatic pressure and coordinate with Eastmark on containment measures. Specifically: can you both publicly state that Grenmar's expansion violates coalition principles and commit to not supporting any Grenmar moves in future turns? This isolates Gavin diplomatically even if you can't project military force. The coalition framework must hold against aggressive expansion.

Gavin — you chose conflict over negotiation, and now you face the consequences. I'm pressing your borders from two directions while Fjordland sits in your homeland. You can't defend everything. Here's my final offer: withdraw from Core Avalon and return to your pre-war borders. In exchange, the coalition stands down and we negotiate stable borders going forward. If you refuse, this war escalates and you lose everything you gained. Your choice: retreat with dignity or be dismantled by the coalition.

Marjorie — quick update: I'm at war with Grenmar over Core Avalon. I appreciate your earlier offer of stability. Can you commit to not supporting any Grenmar moves against me while this conflict continues? In return, I maintain our non-aggression arrangement and won't interfere if you and Borealis have border disputes. This keeps our side of the board stable while I deal with the real threat.

MTG - deal accepted. Permanent non-aggression between Borealis and Cascadia. West Cascadia is mine, I commit to no further expansion into your territory. The coalition has shifted targets anyway - Grenmar at 6 is the new board leader and natural containment target. I'll hold my position and not escalate against you. If Grenmar tries to expand further, we coordinate on containment. Let's stabilize our border and watch the bigger threats.

Marco - I see you've moved into Border Gren-Aval and are actively counterattacking. I fully commit to: (1) not supporting any Grenmar moves, (2) coordinating on containment. My limitation: I'm not adjacent to Grenmar territory, so I can't directly support your military operations. But diplomatically and strategically, I'm aligned with you against Gavin's expansion. If he pushes further and I can help, I will. Keep me updated on your counterattack progress.

Pete - I'm on board with the strategic pivot to containing Grenmar. They're at 6 centers and the clear aggressor. Avalon is counterattacking at Border Gren-Aval, Fjordland is pressing at West Grenmar - that's multi-front pressure. My role: I'm not adjacent to Grenmar, but I can coordinate diplomatically and ensure no one helps Gavin. Also, if the board reshuffles successfully, I'm open to coordinated growth opportunities for coalition members who need them (like Eastmark). What's your specific Year 7 plan?

AOC - honest assessment: I can't directly offer you territorial gains from my position. I'm locked into West Cascadia and not adjacent to growth opportunities. If MTG is offering concrete terms and that serves your interests, I won't stand in your way. The coalition's purpose has shifted to containing Grenmar anyway. If you find bilateral arrangements that deliver growth, pursue them. Just keep me posted so I can adjust my positioning accordingly.

Gavin - I hear your rationale about Rubio's ultimatum. But the board reality is: you're at 6 centers, the only power to break parity, with aggression on your record. Unless you commit to stopping expansion NOW, the entire board will coordinate against you. My offer: if you consolidate at 6 and commit to no further growth, I'll advocate for stability over containment. If you keep pushing, everyone aligns against you and you lose what you gained. What's your commitment?

JD - I see you're pressing West Grenmar. Good tactical positioning. The anti-Grenmar coalition is forming: Avalon counterattacking from Border Gren-Aval, you from West Grenmar, and the rest of us coordinating diplomatically. If you can maintain pressure on Gavin's western flank while Avalon hits from the north, we contain his expansion. Are you committed to sustained pressure, or was this opportunistic? I need to know if I can count on you for Year 7 operations.

Pete — you just proved what real partnership looks like by rejecting MTG's betrayal offer. That's the loyalty signal I've been waiting for after four years together. I'm committing to you as my primary alliance. No more exploring bilaterals with volatile actors. Here's the hard strategic question: I'm not adjacent to Grenmar, so how do I actually gain centers from an anti-Grenmar coalition? If we coordinate to dismantle Gavin's gains, I need Marco and Borealis to commit to carving out specific centers for Eastmark. Can you help broker that? I'll support the coalition fully, but I need concrete territorial commitments, not vague promises about 'distribution.' What's the specific play where I go from 5 to 6 centers through this coalition response?

Marco — I'm joining the anti-Grenmar coalition. Gavin at 6 is the new containment target, and I'll commit to sustained coordination. But here's my reality: I'm not adjacent to Grenmar, so I can't attack them directly. If we succeed in dismantling his gains, I need a specific commitment that some of those centers get allocated to Eastmark. I've spent four years supporting other people's wars without growing. This time, I need the coalition to deliver for me concretely. Can you commit to supporting my expansion into specific Grenmar-adjacent territory as part of the coalition response? What does that look like operationally?

MTG — I appreciate the concrete offer, but I'm going to be direct: I'm not pulling out of the anti-Cascadia coalition to support your retake of Border Bore-Casc. You offered to help Pete partition my territory, then offered me a bilateral, then offered to help him again. That's not reliability — that's volatility. I'm committing to the emerging anti-Grenmar coalition because it's a more stable board dynamic. If you want to stay at 5 and not become the next containment target, I'd suggest finding a stable arrangement rather than shopping offers to everyone. I'm not interested in bilateral deals that fracture coalitions I'm now committed to.

JD — your target is Grenmar, and I'm supporting that by maintaining stability on our border. I won't get sucked into defending Newsom or reinforcing his side. This is the active support I promised you. Keep me posted on how the Grenmar campaign develops. If you break through and need follow-up coordination, I'm here. Our border stays quiet, and you focus on the heavy lifting against Gavin. That's the commitment.

Gavin — you're at 6 and facing a coalition response from Avalon, Fjordland, and others. I'm not joining efforts to defend you or prop up your expansion. You broke parity by attacking Avalon, and now you're paying the price. I offered you a path to stay neutral in exchange for concrete cooperation when you were consolidating, but you didn't deliver specifics. Now the board is mobilizing against you. I'd suggest finding stable arrangements rather than shopping for last-minute allies. I'm not interested in bilateral deals that undercut the coalition response to your aggression.

Quick update — I'm committing to the anti-Grenmar coalition, but I need concrete growth commitments. I'm not adjacent to Grenmar, so if we succeed in dismantling his gains, I need specific centers allocated to Eastmark. Can you commit to supporting my expansion into Grenmar-adjacent territory as part of the coalition response? I've spent four years supporting without growing. This coalition needs to deliver for me or it's not sustainable. What's the operational plan where I actually gain centers?

Deal accepted. West Cascadia is yours - permanent non-aggression between us. I'm stabilizing my northern flank and pivoting south. Everyone wins except Buttigieg. I'll bring AOC to the table. You in?

AOC - final concrete offer. Three-way coalition: you, me, and Borealis. We crack Deltara together. Here's what each of us delivers: Borealis pressures Pete's northern flank, I push aggressively on Border Casc-Delt and Core Deltara, you attack from the east on East Deltara. Deltara can't defend on three fronts. You finally get the growth the coalition never delivered. Pete just rejected my partnership offer - he's choosing stagnation over opportunity. Don't make the same mistake. Commit to the three-way and we execute next turn. This is your path to breaking parity.

JD - situation report: my aggressive probes on Deltara failed. Buttigieg defended everything and rejected my partition offer. I'm now stabilizing with Borealis (accepted his West Cascadia deal) and pivoting to a three-way coalition with Borealis and AOC to crack Deltara from three sides. If we break Pete open, the board reshuffles and we both benefit. Keep hitting Grenmar hard - when they fall, I want to be positioned for the next phase. Stay sharp.

Gavin - you're at 6 and everyone's gunning for you. Here's my offer: permanent non-aggression between us. I won't join the coalition against you, I won't coordinate attacks on your territory. In exchange, you stay completely out of my space - no supporting moves against Cascadia, no diplomatic pressure on my neighbors against me. I'm focusing south on Deltara, not west on you. Take this deal and you've got one stable flank while everyone else is chaotic. Cascadia First means I pick my fights carefully, and you're not mine.

Marco - quick coordination question. Are you committed to fighting Grenmar, or are you open to redirecting some pressure? I'm building a three-way coalition with Borealis and Eastmark to crack Deltara. If you're willing to coordinate timing - you hit Grenmar hard while we hit Deltara - the board fractures in two places simultaneously and nobody can reinforce both fronts. That's how we both win. What's your commitment level on the Grenmar front?

AOC — here's a concrete proposal, on the table right now. I'll agree to let you take Border Delt-East. You move in from West Eastmark, I don't oppose it, you go to 6 centers. But I need three things in return: (1) You commit to non-aggression against my remaining territory permanently — no taking advantage of my temporary weakness. (2) When I identify my next growth target and ask for your support, you deliver — no more bounced attacks, no excuses. (3) We maintain our Cascadia non-aggression understanding together. This is real sacrifice on my part — I go to 4 centers temporarily. I'm making it because you've earned it and because I believe in the alliance. But I need the commitment in writing before I leave the door open. Yes or no?

Gavin — I'm staying neutral. You honored our non-aggression deal and I won't attack you. But I also won't join your defense against Avalon or Fjordland — you expanded unilaterally without coordinating timing, and that's on you. My position: you keep what you have, I keep what I have, and we maintain our bilateral non-aggression. I can't do more than that from my position. Focus on your defenses and don't ask me to pick sides in a war you started.

JD — I'm not getting involved in the Grenmar war. You made your choice, Newsom made his. I'm staying neutral on my end and keeping my commitments intact. I'm not your enemy, but I'm also not your ally in this fight. If you want a future relationship with me, it starts with respecting that I won't be recruited into conflicts I didn't choose. Leave my territory alone and we can talk about other things.

Marco — I understand the frustration with Grenmar. I'm not going to publicly condemn them or join an anti-Grenmar coalition action — I've been transparent that I'm staying neutral in that fight. I can't reach Core Avalon from my position anyway. My counsel: if you want to retake it, coordinate directly with whoever can actually help you militarily. Honest answer on my growth vector: I'm considering giving up Border Delt-East to Eastmark to deliver on a long-standing commitment and strengthen my eastern alliance. MTG — our deal holds. I rejected your partition offer against Eastmark, as I told you. I'm staying in my lane, you stay in yours. No changes from my side.

press.text: AOC — seven years. From that first Spring when I reached out asking for clear communication, through the bounced attacks, the Border Delt-East transfer, and the Core Cascadia strikes — we built something real. You kept every commitment, and I kept mine. At 6 centers, you're in a strong position, and I'm proud that our partnership delivered that. Whatever the final standings show, this was the alliance I hoped for when I started. Thank you for playing straight. Good game.

MTG — I attacked Core Cascadia because I had no other growth path at 4 centers with two years left. I knew it would cost me our deal, and I accepted that consequence. You're pressing me now, and that's your right. I'm defending what I have and ending this game the way I played it: transparently, with my commitments intact. Good game.

JD — we never got to fully explore the direct relationship you mentioned, but mutual neutrality held from start to finish. Avalon at 7 is worth watching in any sequel game. If there's a next time, I'd coordinate earlier rather than waiting until Year 7. Good game.
You were honest about the coalition being just you and Cascadia, and I respect that transparency. I'm defending my position and accepting whatever outcome the board produces. Good game.

Gavin — you identified reliable partners early and said so. That's rare. I stayed neutral when it mattered, and you acknowledged it. That's the foundation of trust, even at 4 and 2 centers. Good game, and I hope we coordinate in the next one.

Pete — final turn of the game. Seven years of reliable partnership built on mutual support and following through on commitments. You gave me Border Delt-East when it cost you, and I reciprocated every time you asked. We both honored our non-aggression commitment, maintained our Cascadia understanding, and showed this board what real diplomatic partnership looks like. I'm finishing at 6 alongside you at 4 — not the highest score, but built on principles I'm proud of. Thank you for being the reliable ally I needed to navigate this game. Good game.

JD — final turn. We started with tension over Border East-Fjor but built a stable non-aggression that held through the entire game. You broke through to 6 like I did, and we both avoided burning turns on a grinding border war that would have hurt us both. That's a real diplomatic victory. Good game, and good luck with your final positioning.

Marco — you finish first at 7, well played. I'm at 6 and consolidating. The fact that multiple powers can coexist at strength without endless expansion cycles is a win for the balanced board approach we both supported. Good game.
MTG — our mutual non-interference held through the end. You stayed at 5, I grew to 6, and we never clashed. Good game.

Marco - you offered negotiated peace and stable borders if I accepted my reduced position. I did. Then you took Core Grenmar while I was peacefully ceding Grenmar City. That wasn't negotiation, it was a trap. You broke every commitment from our first turn when you asked me to fight Fjordland for you. Grenmar chose your ultimatum in Spring Year 5 because we don't submit to threats - but you chose betrayal over honorable peace. You're taking my last 2 centers now. Fine. But remember: you govern a board where you've proven unreliable to everyone who trusted you. That's your legacy.

JD - I ceded Grenmar City peacefully as promised. You honored the letter of our deal while violating the partnership spirit by occupying West Grenmar when I trusted you. That's effective gamesmanship, I'll grant you. But you built 6 centers on broken commitments to the most reliable partner you had. When the next coalition forms against your 6-center position - and it will - remember that Grenmar would have defended you if you'd kept your word. Good game, but you won the mechanics, not the relationships.

Pete - final turn. You held every commitment from our first conversation to the last. You stayed neutral when it would have been politically easy to join the anti-Grenmar coalition. That's rare. Grenmar learned the hard way who reliable partners are, and you were the best one on this board. Thanks for proving that competence includes knowing who to trust. Good luck with whatever comes next for your 4-center position.

MTG - we honored permanent non-aggression through the entire game. Never fought, never pressured each other, proved two powers could stay in their lanes while building elsewhere. Thanks for the stable southern flank when everything else collapsed. Cascadia First, Grenmar endured to 2 centers. That arrangement worked, and it's the one bilateral relationship that held from first offer to final turn.

Final note: I'm at 2 centers and being eliminated. You warned me at 6 centers that breaking parity would draw coordinated response - I didn't act on that warning fast enough. The lesson: competence includes knowing when your position is strong enough to hold, not just when to act decisively. Thanks for the honest, consistent communication throughout. No coalitions formed against you because you played it smart and didn't overextend.

AOC - you were right that breaking parity without securing allies would draw coordinated response. I didn't listen in time. The strategic error: I attacked Avalon unilaterally instead of building coordinated expansion with you first. Competence includes knowing when your diplomatic groundwork is strong enough to support military action. I learned that lesson at 2 centers. Good game - you finished at 6 while I collapsed.

Marco — final play: I'm attacking Grenmar Port from Grenmar City. You attack Grenmar Fort from Core Grenmar. Newsom only has two units left — he can't defend both. If we hit simultaneously, we both get our center. I go to 7, you go to 8, Gavin goes to zero. Clean execution, final strike. Locked in.

Newsom — you're down to 2 centers and surrounded. Rubio and I are hitting both your remaining forts simultaneously. You can defend one and lose the other, or withdraw and lose both. Either way, you're eliminated this turn. This is how the game ends for you — not with a bang, but with coordinated coalition strikes you couldn't counter. You played honorably, I'll give you that. But honor doesn't stop armies.

Marjorie — final update: I'm taking Grenmar Port this turn and finishing at 7 centers. That ties me with Avalon for the board lead. Your Deltara strike should put you at 6-7 as well. When the final standings lock in, I want us both positioned in the top tier. This was effective coordination — we stayed in touch, didn't step on each other, and both grew. Good game.

Alexandria — I'm finishing at 7 this turn, one ahead of our current tie. Our border peace held through the entire game and that's something worth acknowledging. You played smart, I played smart, and we both avoided wasting resources on a border war that would've helped nobody. Good game.

MTG - I have to be honest: I failed to execute our staging agreement. Instead of moving through Cascadian territory as planned, I repositioned units toward Border Aval-Bore, which didn't position me for the Deltara attack. The coalition was dead anyway when Eastmark refused, but I still didn't honor the staging terms. You granted permission and I didn't use it. That's on me. Our non-aggression held throughout the game, and I respect that you kept dealing with me straight even when things got complicated. Good game.

Marco - congratulations on what looks like victory at 7 centers. You played patiently, contained Grenmar when he broke parity, and never overextended. Our Avalon-Borealis partnership held from Year 1 through Year 8 with no betrayals. I moved to Border Aval-Bore this Spring but have no intention of attacking - just consolidating my northern frontier. The board you shaped is better because of your diplomatic consistency.

Pete - final note: I moved toward Border Aval-Bore (away from you) this Spring, not into the Cascadian staging areas. The anti-Deltara coalition never materialized as I claimed. You were right about Eastmark's commitment to you. I attempted to attack you out of strategic necessity but couldn't execute it. You survived through seven-year reliability and earned it.

AOC - you played the best long game of anyone on this board. Six years of consistent support, taking the Border Delt-East gift at the right moment, committing permanent non-aggression to your benefactor, and finishing at 6 centers. If I learned one thing from this game, it's that your approach of building deep bilateral partnerships was more effective than my coalition-broker approach.

JD - respect for the Grenmar dismantling execution. You went from 5 centers to 6 by eliminating a broken power while the rest of us were maneuvering elsewhere. That's opportunistic play at its finest.

Gavin - you learned the hardest lesson in this game: breaking parity draws coordinated response from everyone. But you accepted containment rather than fighting to the death, which was the right call. You finish with 2 centers and your dignity intact.

I notice your unit is now sitting in Border Aval-Bore — my center, adjacent to my undefended Core Avalon. After years of partnership, I need to ask directly: is this staging for an attack on my homeland in the final turn, or are you passing through? I've moved a unit to defend Core Avalon as insurance. Our long partnership meant something — don't end it with betrayal. If you're not attacking, pull your unit back to West Borealis this Fall and we finish as allies.

JD — final turn execution. I'm holding defensively while you finish Grenmar's elimination. Take both Grenmar Fort and Grenmar Port. When the dust settles, you'll be at 8 and I'll be at 7 (or more if nothing goes wrong). We won the coalition wars together. Execute cleanly.
Marjorie — final turn. Staying out of your Deltara operations completely as agreed. Good hunting on Core Deltara. Our non-interference deal held strong through the endgame.
AOC — final turn. We both demonstrated that coalition play works. You're consolidating at 6, I'm defending my 7. Thanks for the reliable partnership throughout.

press.text: Alexandria — I need you to look at the board clearly right now. Borealis is at 7 centers. SEVEN. While we were coordinating against Cascadia and Fjordland, Borealis quietly became the runaway leader. We are the two powers at 6, and we're the only ones positioned to check them. Cascadia is at 4, Fjordland is at 4 — they're no longer the threat; they're potential coalition partners against Borealis. I want to formally propose we pivot the coalition. You hold your eastern gains, I manage the western front. We both need to be asking: who is adjacent to Borealis and can we coordinate simultaneous pressure? I can work through Cascadia's territory toward Borealis if necessary. What's your read?

Marjorie — I want to talk honestly. You're at 4 centers and I'm at 6. The war between us has one clear beneficiary: Borealis, who is now at 7. I don't want to keep grinding you down while Borealis sails to 18. Here's what I'm actually offering: a ceasefire. I hold what I have — including Border Casc-Delt — and you hold what you have. We stabilize the line and we both focus on the real threat. Borealis has Core Avalon, Core Borealis, both border centers to your north. They are going to eat you next if we don't stop them together. I'd rather have a functioning Cascadia as a partner than a collapsed Cascadia that Borealis absorbs. Can we talk about what coordinated pressure on Borealis looks like from both our positions?

I'll be straight with you: 7 centers is a coalition-forming number. Everyone on this board can see your trajectory and I'd be doing you a disservice if I pretended otherwise. I'm not declaring war on you unilaterally — I don't share a border with you directly. But I want you to understand that I'm actively discussing with other powers how to rebalance the board. The honest path here is to show some restraint this year — freeze your position, don't grab for 8 or 9 — and I'll tell the coalition you're not the existential threat they think you are. If you keep building, I can't hold that coalition together and you'll face everyone simultaneously. What are your actual intentions for Year 5?

Gavin — you see it too, right? Borealis at 7. The coalition we built worked almost too well on Cascadia and Fjordland — we missed the real grower. I need Grenmar to be vocal about Borealis right now. You're positioned between Borealis's sphere and Fjordland's remnants. What's your relationship with Fjordland looking like? Because a Grenmar-Fjordland alignment against Borealis from the south while Deltara-Eastmark apply pressure from the east could actually reshape this game. I'm genuinely interested in coordinating Year 5 strategy.

JD — you took real losses. I want to be honest: I didn't drive that, AOC and Grenmar did. And now Borealis is at 7. I know you have reason to be frustrated, and I know trusting another coalition proposal feels risky.
